findings.issue_text: [BUG] minimumTokenResponseSchema uses computed object keys `[z.string().toString()]` and `[z.string().optional().toString()]`, which evaluate to the literal string produced by ZodType's toString (e.g. '[object Object]'), not 'any property'. When APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED is on, every credential sync token refresh fails safeParse (real payloads have keys like expiry_date, not the literal garbage key) and the function throws 'Invalid refreshed tokens were returned', breaking Google/Zoom/Office365/Salesforce token refresh entirely for self-hosters who enable the feature.

[BUG] parseRefreshTokenResponse assigns the literal string "refresh_token" to refreshTokenResponse.data.refresh_token when the parsed schema (minimumTokenResponseSchema) has no refresh_token field. The caller then persists the credential with refresh_token literally set to "refresh_token", so the next token refresh sends the string 'refresh_token' to Google/Zoom/Office365/Salesforce OAuth endpoints and every subsequent refresh (and every booking using that credential) fails.

[BUG] GoogleCalendarService assigns `const key = parseRefreshTokenResponse(googleCredentials, googleCredentialSchema)` — the function returns the Zod safeParse result object ({success, data, error}), not the parsed credential — and stores that wrapper directly via `prisma.credential.update({ data: { key } })`. The credential key in the DB becomes `{success:true,data:{...}}` instead of the flat token object, so the next GoogleCalendarService construction fails googleCredentialSchema.parse on the stored key and all Google Calendar bookings for that user break.

[BUG] In sync mode refreshOAuthTokens returns a fetch Response (no `.data` property), but GoogleCalendarService reads `const token = res?.data` from it. token is undefined and `token.access_token` throws TypeError, so any Google refresh path that takes the CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT branch crashes at runtime instead of updating tokens.

[BUG] In sync mode refreshOAuthTokens returns a fetch Response, but the code immediately reads `zohoCrmTokenInfo.data.error` and `zohoCrmTokenInfo.data.expiryDate`. Response has no `.data` property, so `zohoCrmTokenInfo.data.error` throws TypeError on the very first Zoho CRM token refresh when credential sync is enabled — the feature path never works for Zoho CRM.

[BUG] The Bigin code reads `tokenInfo.data.error` / `tokenInfo.data` from the return of refreshOAuthTokens, which in sync mode is a fetch Response with no `.data`; additionally the third argument `credentialId` is passed but the surrounding code only defines `credentialKey`/`credential`-derived values, not a `credentialId` in scope. Sync mode crashes with TypeError on `.data`; and if `credentialId` is not defined in this scope the module fails TypeScript compilation outright, breaking the build for all consumers of this package.

[BUG] The result of refreshOAuthTokens is typed and consumed as HubspotToken (e.g. hubspotRefreshToken.refresh_token / expiry fields), but in sync mode it is a fetch Response object whose properties are body/bodyUsed/headers, not OAuth token fields. hubspotRefreshToken.refresh_token and friends are undefined in sync mode, so the HubSpot credential is persisted with undefined access token and garbage expiry, and all subsequent HubSpot API calls fail with 401.

[BUG] The new unconditional Salesforce refresh gate checks `response.statusText !== "OK"`, but statusText is a human-readable reason phrase that many clients/proxies/servers do not set (and can be localized or empty for a 200 response). A 200 response with statusText '' (e.g. behind some proxies/HTTP2 stacks where reason phrases are dropped) throws HttpError 400 even though the refresh succeeded, breaking every Salesforce calendar operation for those deployments.

[ADVISORY] The constructor now performs a blocking remote POST to login.salesforce.com and a Prisma credential.update on every SalesforceCalendarService instantiation, where previously jsforce.Connection refreshed tokens lazily only when an access token expired. Every Salesforce calendar operation (and every booking touching Salesforce) now pays an extra OAuth round-trip plus a DB write per instantiation — a hot-path regression and a new network failure point that turns previously-cached-token operations into hard failures when Salesforce is slow or rate-limits.

[ADVISORY] The office365 refresh path previously logged the zod error and MS response on parse failure before continuing; parseRefreshTokenResponse throws instead, and the success/error branch and console.error were deleted, so `tokenResponse.success` is always true at the spread site while a failed parse now propagates as an unhandled generic Error('Invalid refreshed tokens were returned'). Operators debugging Office365 token refresh issues lose the MS response payload from logs; a transient malformed MS response that previously degraded gracefully now crashes the booking request with a stack trace and no diagnostic data.

[ADVISORY] APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED is typed as `string | undefined` (the && of two env strings), not a boolean, so every `if (APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED && ...)` and the webhook's `if (!APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED)` rely on implicit truthiness of a non-empty string. If either env var is set to a whitespace or placeholder value (e.g. copied from .env.example as `""` is left but a space is pasted in), the flag silently flips on and all token refreshes route to the (broken) sync path; a boolean coercion or explicit check would fail fast instead.

[BUG] parseRefreshTokenResponse throws a generic Error when safeParse fails, but in non-sync mode it receives full typed schemas (e.g. googleCredentialSchema) that include fields like refresh_token — so a partially-populated refresh response that previously failed only the strict parse now either passes the minimum schema (sync mode) or crashes the request with an unhandled error instead of the caller's previous graceful handling (see office365 deleted error-logging branch). Zoom and Google refresh paths that previously handled safeParse failure inline (zoom's parsedToken.success check, office365's logged-continue) now throw before that check is reachable, converting degraded-but-logged cases into 500s during booking.

[BUG] minimumTokenResponseSchema uses computed object keys `[z.string().toString()]`, which evaluate to the literal key "ZodString" (or similar), so the schema does not allow arbitrary extra properties like refresh_token, expiry_date, or scope at all. When credential sharing is enabled, every provider refresh response is parsed against a schema requiring a property literally named "ZodString" to be a number and permitting nothing else; zod's default strips unknown keys, so parsed data contains only access_token (and drops refresh_token, expiry_date, instance_url, etc.), which callers then read as undefined — Google reads token.expiry_date as undefined and Zoho/Salesforce lose instance_url, producing broken credentials written to the DB.

[BUG] The function unconditionally replaces a missing refresh_token with the placeholder string "refresh_token" before the parsed result is persisted to prisma.credential by callers. In sharing mode, minimumTokenResponseSchema (see above) never yields a refresh_token, so every refresh overwrites the user's stored real refresh_token with the literal "refresh_token"; the next refresh attempt (and any fallback to the provider's real endpoint) sends "refresh_token" as the grant, permanently bricking the integration until the user re-authorizes.

[BUG] In sharing mode refreshOAuthTokens returns a raw fetch Response, but the Hubspot, Zoho Bigin, Zoho CRM and Google callers expect provider-specific shapes (hubspot client object with fields, axios response with `.data`, google `{res:{data}}`). When CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT is set, hubspot's `hubspotRefreshToken.refresh_token`, zoho's `tokenInfo.data.error`, and google's `res?.data` all read undefined/throw TypeError on a fetch Response (which has no `.data`), crashing every booking that touches those integrations instead of refreshing tokens.

[BUG] APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED gates the feature on only CALCOM_WEBHOOK_SECRET and CALCOM_APP_CREDENTIAL_ENCRYPTION_KEY, omitting the sibling flag CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT that refreshOAuthTokens additionally requires, leaving two inconsistent definitions of "enabled" on the same touched credential path. A self-hoster who sets the webhook secret and encryption key but not (or mis-spells) the sync endpoint gets the webhook endpoint active (accepting and overwriting credentials for any user id) while token refresh silently falls back to the provider endpoint — i.e., the feature appears enabled in one half of the path and disabled in the other, with no validation or error telling the operator which flag is missing.

[BUG] APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED is `env && env`, which evaluates to a string (or undefined), not a boolean; it is exported from a constants module full of boolean flags and consumed in boolean contexts. Consumers get a truthy string (e.g. the secret value) wherever they expect `true`; any future use in a strict boolean context (zod boolean schema, a boolean API field, `=== true` check) silently misfires, and the exported value leaks the raw secret string into anything that serializes the flag.

[BUG] The handler calls appCredentialWebhookRequestBodySchema.parse (throwing .parse, not safeParse) and has no HTTP method check, so malformed bodies and GET requests fall through to an unhandled ZodError. A caller POSTing an invalid payload (or hitting the endpoint with GET) receives a 500 from the framework's unhandled error instead of the 4xx the endpoint's own validation contract promises, and repeated bad requests generate error-alert noise indistinguishable from real failures.

[BUG] The webhook accepts an arbitrary userId and appSlug and overwrites that user's stored credential key with attacker-supplied decrypted JSON without any check that the key matches the app's expected credential schema. Anyone holding the single shared CALCOM_WEBHOOK_SECRET (one secret for all apps and all users, no per-caller scoping) can replace any user's app credential with arbitrary keys of the wrong shape; downstream CalendarService code then reads undefined fields from the key and every booking for that user fails, with no audit trail distinguishing webhook-written credentials from OAuth-written ones.

[ADVISORY] The Salesforce refresh is hard-coded as an unconditional fetch to login.salesforce.com in the service constructor and is not routed through refreshOAuthTokens like every other integration in this diff, so the feature silently does not cover Salesforce. Self-hosters using credential sync get Salesforce refreshing against the provider endpoint with local app keys that may not exist on their instance (this is the exact scenario the feature exists for); additionally the network call now fires on every service construction even when the stored access token is still valid, and the `response.statusText !== "OK"` check is fragile under HTTP/2 (statusText is empty) so valid responses will be rejected with a 400.

[ADVISORY] zoho-bigin passes `credentialId` to refreshOAuthTokens' `userId` parameter while every other call site passes `credential.userId`. If `credentialId` is the numeric credential id rather than the user id, the sync endpoint receives the wrong identifier (or undefined, silently disabling sync for zoho-bigin), so zoho-bigin credentials either sync under the wrong user or never sync at all — inconsistent with the sibling call sites in the same diff.

[ADVISORY] The diff removes the branch that logged zod errors on failed refresh-token parses (relying on parseRefreshTokenResponse's throw instead) but keeps persisting the credential with `tokenResponse.success && tokenResponse.data` spread, mixing a throwing helper with a non-throwing spread pattern left over from the old safeParse flow. A maintainer reading the code sees both a throw-on-failure helper and dead `success &&` guard logic; the next change here is riskier because the two failure-handling styles coexist in one function, and the diagnostic context (raw MS response) that used to be logged is now lost, making production refresh failures undiagnosable.

[ADVISORY] The diff adds a new authenticated write API endpoint and two new shared OAuth utilities (refreshOAuthTokens, parseRefreshTokenResponse) that alter the token-refresh path of eight integrations, with zero test files or assertions anywhere in the diff (no spec/test/itest-shaped file appears in the changed paths). A regression in the placeholder refresh_token mutation or the raw-Response return type (both present in this diff) would break every booking on the affected integrations and ship undetected; there is no verification of the webhook's auth rejection, schema validation, or create-vs-update branch, and no fixture proving the sync endpoint contract (fetch body shape, response shape) matches what all eight call sites expect.

[ADVISORY] The fetch to CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT sends no authentication header, no Content-Type, and no timeout or error handling; the sync response is also a parallel hand-maintained contract with the webhook handler on the other side, with no shared schema as a single source of truth. Any operator who exposes the sync endpoint (as .env.example instructs) has an unauthenticated POST accepting calcomUserId/appSlug; and because the request/response shape exists only as comments in two files, the next edit to one side (e.g. adding the webhook secret header) drifts silently from the other, failing at runtime only during a live token refresh in a booking flow.

[BUG] minimumTokenResponseSchema uses computed keys `[z.string().toString()]` and `[z.string().optional().toString()]`, which evaluate to the literal property name `[object Object]`-style strings, making the schema require a mandatory numeric property that no real OAuth token response ever contains. When APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED and CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT are set, every safeParse fails, parseRefreshTokenResponse throws 'Invalid refreshed tokens were returned', and token refresh (and thus every calendar/video operation using those credentials) breaks for Google, Office365, Zoom, and Salesforce users.

[BUG] parseRefreshTokenResponse unconditionally (in both the credential-sharing and the default path) replaces a missing refresh_token with the literal string "refresh_token" before the parsed object is persisted as the credential key. On the default (non-sync) path for apps whose refresh responses legitimately omit refresh_token (e.g. some providers rotate only access tokens), the credential key is silently overwritten with a bogus refresh_token; the next refresh attempt sends the literal string 'refresh_token' to the provider and fails permanently — a behavior change to unrelated flows not required by the credential-sync feature.

[BUG] When credential sharing is enabled, full per-app schema validation (zoomRefreshedTokenSchema, refreshTokenResponseSchema, googleCredentialSchema, salesforceTokenSchema) is discarded in favor of the broken minimum schema, so garbage or malformed token payloads are accepted whenever they contain an access_token. A credential-sync endpoint returning malformed data (missing instance_url for Salesforce, expiry_date for Google, etc.) passes validation, corrupt credentials get persisted via prisma.credential.update, and subsequent API calls fail in provider-specific ways instead of being rejected at refresh time — validation weakened on the sync path with no requirement justifying it.

[BUG] The Salesforce CalendarService constructor now performs an unconditional eager token refresh fetch to login.salesforce.com on every instantiation, replacing the previous jsforce-managed refresh flow; this work is not traceable to the stated 'credential sync' intent and runs even when APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED is false. Every Salesforce calendar operation now adds a blocking network round-trip (and a DB write) on the hot path even for standard self-hosted installs with no credential sharing configured; a Salesforce outage or 429 on the token endpoint now fails calendar reads/writes that previously used the cached access token via jsforce.

[BUG] The new eager refresh checks `response.statusText !== "OK"` but Salesforce returns HTTP 200 with statusText "" (HTTP/2 has no reason phrase, and Node fetch populates statusText from the response), so non-2xx bodies are not the only failure this misses; additionally the refreshed key persisted via prisma.credential.update drops refresh_token context when accessTokenParsed comes from the broken minimum schema (no refresh_token field), storing a credential whose key lacks refresh_token unless re-added. On any Salesforce instantiation where the refresh response lacks refresh_token (always, per RFC refresh responses), the persisted key omits refresh_token except where the 'refresh_token' placeholder hack re-inserts the literal string, breaking the next refresh for all Salesforce users.

[BUG] refreshOAuthTokens is called with `credentialId` (a credential identifier string) as the third parameter, which the function treats as the cal.com userId sent to the credential-sync endpoint. When credential sync is enabled, the sync endpoint receives a credential UUID string in the calcomUserId field instead of a numeric user id, so the parent application cannot resolve the user and Zoho Bigin token refresh fails for every Bigin user under the feature this PR claims to implement.

[BUG] The sync branch returns the raw `fetch` Response whose body is whatever the credential-sync endpoint produces (documented as 'only the access token and expiry date'), but every call site (Lark, Zoom, Webex, Office365, Zoho) immediately consumes the response with provider-specific parsing/handleErrors helpers, and the Google call site reads `res?.data` off the Response object. In sync mode Google Calendar reads `token.access_token` from a fetch Response (undefined) and assigns undefined into googleCredentials, and provider-specific error handlers run against the sync endpoint's payload shape; the 'app integration enhancement' path is untested against any of the actual consuming code and diverges from every call site's expected contract.

[ADVISORY] The webhook handler is scoped to accept updates for any userId and any app slug with only a shared-secret check; no per-app or per-user authorization, no HTTP method check, and string equality on the secret instead of constant-time comparison. Anyone who obtains the single shared CALCOM_WEBHOOK_SECRET (which is also used, per .env.example, for the parent application) can overwrite any user's stored OAuth credentials for any app, silently swapping calendar/video credentials; operators enabling the feature expose a credential-overwrite primitive with no audit trail.

[ADVISORY] The keys payload is decrypted with `process.env.CALCOM_APP_CREDENTIAL_ENCRYPTION_KEY || ""` and the result is JSON.parse'd with no try/catch and no schema validation of the decrypted key object before persisting it as the credential key. A request with a valid secret but malformed ciphertext (or an unset encryption key, which APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED only weakly guards via string-truthiness) causes symmetricDecrypt/JSON.parse to throw, returning a 500 and writing no useful log, and if it does parse it persists an arbitrary JSON blob as a credential key that downstream services will fail to cast.

[ADVISORY] The credential-sync branch does not send the refresh token or any per-app OAuth context (only calcomUserId and appSlug) to the sync endpoint, so the contract relies entirely on the parent application holding the actual OAuth client secret and refresh token — yet the webhook handler in this same PR persists key objects created from this flow. Two hand-maintained halves of a protocol (the sync fetch body and the app-credential webhook payload) evolve independently with no shared schema; a self-hoster implementing the documented endpoint must guess the response shape, and any mismatch is only discovered as runtime failures in provider-specific code paths.

[ADVISORY] The redirect URI is changed from `appConfig.slug` to the hardcoded literal "zoho-bigin", an unrelated behavioral edit smuggled into an import-path refactor. If appConfig.slug ever diverges from the hardcoded string (or this handler is reused for a differently-slugged deployment), the OAuth redirect URI silently mismatches the registered callback and Zoho Bigin installs break; the change is not traceable to the credential-sync requirement and should be reverted or justified in the PR description.

[ADVISORY] The diff removes the existing console.error diagnostics for zod validation failures of the refreshed Office365 token, replacing them with the shared parseRefreshTokenResponse which throws a bare 'Invalid refreshed tokens were returned' Error. Office365 operators debugging expired/malformed Microsoft token responses lose the zodError details and the raw MS response from logs, making refresh failures in production significantly harder to diagnose on both the sync and non-sync paths.

[ADVISORY] HubSpot and Lark call sites route their refresh through refreshOAuthTokens but do not apply parseRefreshTokenResponse, while Google, Zoom, Office365 and Salesforce do — the refactor's coverage is inconsistent across apps for the same stated feature. In sync mode HubSpot/Lark receive whatever shape the sync endpoint returns with no validation at all (minimum or otherwise), so a misconfigured sync endpoint corrupts HubSpot/Lark credentials silently while the same misconfiguration is caught (loudly) for the other apps; the next maintainer must reverse-engineer which apps got which half of the feature.

[ADVISORY] APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED is derived as the string-truthy AND of CALCOM_WEBHOOK_SECRET and CALCOM_APP_CREDENTIAL_ENCRYPTION_KEY but excludes CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT, and an empty-string env var (the .env.example default) is falsy while a whitespace value silently enables the feature. Operators setting only the sync endpoint and webhook secret (per a partial reading of the .env.example block) get no sync and no warning, while a stray non-empty placeholder value in one of the two keys flips refresh behavior for every OAuth app in the instance, including replacing schema validation with the broken minimum schema — a feature toggle hidden behind two unrelated env vars with no explicit enable switch.

[BUG] The computed-key schema produces only the literal key "[object Object]" (both `z.string().toString()` and `z.string().optional().toString()` evaluate to the same string, and the second overwrites the first), so minimumTokenResponseSchema accepts only {access_token} and the comment's 'any property with a number is the expiry' is not implemented. When credential-sharing is enabled, every refreshed-token payload parsed by this schema is stripped to {access_token} (Zod strips unknown keys), so expiry and all other token fields are silently dropped, and callers persist a near-empty credential to the DB.

[BUG] Because the minimum schema never captures refresh_token (unknown keys are stripped), `refreshTokenResponse.data.refresh_token` is always undefined and the code unconditionally overwrites it with the sentinel string "refresh_token". In Google CalendarService.ts (line ~99) this stripped object is persisted as the credential key via prisma.credential.update, permanently destroying the user's real refresh_token and all other credential fields; the OAuth credential can never be refreshed again and the integration is bricked for that user.

[BUG] The code reads `const token = res?.data` but in credential-sharing mode refreshOAuthTokens returns a raw fetch Response, which has no `data` property, so token is undefined and `token.access_token` throws TypeError. Every Google Calendar token refresh on a credential-sharing deployment crashes before persisting, taking down booking calendar operations with an unhandled TypeError instead of refreshing the token.

[BUG] refreshOAuthTokens is called with `credentialId` instead of `credential.userId` (confusable pair: both numbers in scope, wrong one bound), so the sync endpoint receives a credential ID where its contract (calcomUserId) specifies a user ID. When credential-sharing is enabled, the parent application looks up the wrong entity by credential-id-as-user-id, returning the wrong user's tokens or a 404, silently corrupting Bigin credential refresh.

[BUG] In sharing mode refreshOAuthTokens returns a raw fetch Response, but the code types the result as HubspotToken and later accesses properties of the hubspotClient's token object (e.g. .refresh_token, .expires_in) directly on it. In sharing mode the Hubspot refresh path reads undefined properties off a Response object, producing NaN expiry and a broken credential instead of a refreshed token — the integration shape (axios-like client result vs fetch Response) is not representable by the shared return type.

[BUG] In sharing mode refreshOAuthTokens returns a fetch Response while the surrounding code treats the result as an axios response and reads `tokenInfo.data`, which is undefined on a Response. Bigin token refresh in sharing mode crashes on `tokenInfo.data.error`/`tokenInfo.data.access_token` access (undefined), so Bigin calendar operations fail on every shared deployment.

[BUG] The webhook writes the decrypted keys object to `credential.key` in plaintext, while every read path decrypts credential.key with CALENDSO_ENCRYPTION_KEY (the app credential readers in app-store call symmetricDecrypt on credential.key), so synced credentials and locally-created credentials have incompatible encodings stored in the same column. Any credential created or updated via this sync webhook fails to decrypt in the consuming app services, so the synced integration is unusable; the data model has two formats in one column with no discriminator.

[BUG] The constructor path now performs an unconditional token refresh POST to login.salesforce.com on every service instantiation, even when credential-sharing is disabled and the existing token is still valid, and stores `key` as the parsed minimal/salesforceTokenSchema result merged only with refresh_token — dropping any fields not in salesforceTokenSchema (e.g. expiry tracking fields) that previously lived in credential.key. Every Salesforce calendar/video operation now pays a blocking remote OAuth round-trip (hot-path regression: jsforce previously refreshed lazily on 401), and in sharing mode parseRefreshTokenResponse strips the response to {access_token}, so the persisted key loses instance_url/signature/id that jsforce needs — the connection becomes unusable on the next invocation.

[BUG] In sharing mode parseRefreshTokenResponse parses responseBody with the broken minimum schema, so parsedToken.data contains only {access_token, refresh_token:"refresh_token"} and the Zoom credential update persists that garbage. The real Zoom refresh_token is overwritten with the literal string "refresh_token", permanently breaking token refresh for Zoom on credential-sharing deployments.

[BUG] The shared-path fetch has no timeout, no response.ok check, no error handling, and returns a raw Response regardless of what each caller's non-shared path returns (fetch Response, axios response, hubspot client object), with the sharing gate duplicated as a raw env-var check (process.env.CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT) at every call site with no single flag constant. A slow or failed credential-sync endpoint cascades into every calendar/video refresh with an unbounded hang (no degradation), and any caller whose native library returns a non-fetch shape (Hubspot, Zoho Bigin/CRM axios) reads undefined fields — a shared-dependency failure takes down all synced integrations simultaneously.

[BUG] The webhook secret comparison reads req.headers[process.env.CALCOM_WEBHOOK_HEADER_NAME] with no case normalization of the configured header name; Node lowercases header keys, so any operator who sets CALCOM_WEBHOOK_HEADER_NAME with uppercase letters (the .env.example only says 'Should be in lowercase' in a comment) gets a header lookup that never matches. The webhook returns 403 for every legitimate sync request when the env var contains uppercase characters, silently disabling credential sync with no error surfaced beyond a forbidden response.

[BUG] refreshOAuthTokens is passed the appSlug "msteams" but the corresponding office365calendar service uses "office365-calendar" while both use the same parent-application credential store, creating two slugs for what the parent app must treat as one Microsoft integration with one set of app keys. A parent application syncing Microsoft credentials sees the same user's Microsoft credential under two different slugs, so syncing 'office365-calendar' does not cover the msteams video path and vice versa — MS Teams video calls fail to refresh in sharing mode.

[ADVISORY] The function name and parameter promise schema-pluggability but in sharing mode the caller-provided schema is discarded entirely (minimumTokenResponseSchema wins), a parallel hidden branch that contradicts the signature contract `parseRefreshTokenResponse(response, schema)`. The next developer adding expiry/refresh_token validation to a per-app schema will see their validation silently ignored on shared deployments, and failures that the schema would have caught (missing expiry) pass green while the stored credential is unusable — a stand-in guard that goes green while the real contract is broken.

[BUG] The minimumTokenResponseSchema uses computed keys `[z.string().toString()]` and `[z.string().optional().toString()]`, which evaluate to literal property names "z.string()"/"z.string().optional()" rather than validating arbitrary token fields, so the schema only enforces access_token and validates nothing else. When APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED, any provider response — including malformed ones missing refresh_token, expiry, or with wrong types — passes validation, and garbage credentials get persisted to the DB.

[BUG] When the parsed data lacks refresh_token, the code assigns the literal string "refresh_token" as the refresh token (`refreshTokenResponse.data.refresh_token = "refresh_token"`). Google Calendar, Office365 and Zoom persist the literal string "refresh_token" into prisma.credential, permanently destroying the user's real refresh token; the next access-token expiry makes the integration unrecoverable without re-auth.

[BUG] refreshOAuthTokens in sync mode returns a raw fetch Response from CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT, but this call site assigns it to `hubspotRefreshToken: HubspotToken` and then reads `.expires_in`/`.refresh_token` off it, which are undefined on a Response object. With credential sync enabled, every HubSpot token refresh computes NaN expiry and writes a corrupt credential key, breaking the integration.

[BUG] In sync mode refreshOAuthTokens returns a raw fetch Response, but the code does `const token = res?.data` expecting the google-auth-library result shape (`.res.data`), so `token` is undefined and `token.access_token` throws TypeError. With credential sync enabled, every Google Calendar access-token refresh crashes on `token.access_token`, breaking calendar operations entirely.

[BUG] The custom sync endpoint fetch has no Authorization header or webhook secret and returns a raw Response object that every call site then consumes as the provider-specific token shape (axios response, google res object, provider JSON), a contract no call site was written for. The sync-enabled code path is non-functional for Lark, Office365, Office365 Video, Webex, Zoom and Zoho adapters as well; consumers call provider-specific handlers (handleZoomResponse, handleLarkError) or read `.data`/`.expires_in` on a plain Response.

[BUG] refreshOAuthTokens is called with `credentialId` as the third argument, but the function signature is `userId: number | null` and the sync path sends it as `calcomUserId` in the POST body. With credential sync enabled, the parent application receives a credential ID as calcomUserId, so it either fails the user lookup or syncs tokens to the wrong user.

[BUG] The constructor now unconditionally POSTs to login.salesforce.com/services/oauth2/token to refresh tokens on every instantiation of SalesforceCalendarService, replacing jsforce's on-demand refresh-on-401 behavior, and overwrites the stored credential key on every call. Every Salesforce calendar operation (including reads with a valid unexpired access token) makes an extra network round-trip to Salesforce, and concurrent calls race to overwrite the credential row; if Salesforce rate-limits or the refresh fails, previously-working calendar access now fails.

[BUG] parseRefreshTokenResponse throws `new Error("Invalid refreshed tokens were returned")` on parse failure, replacing the previous behavior which logged the zod error and MS response and continued with `tokenResponse.success && tokenResponse.data`. Office365 token responses that previously degraded gracefully (logged, keys updated with whatever parsed) now abort the whole refreshAccessToken with an unhandled error, breaking booking flows that previously succeeded.

[BUG] symmetricDecrypt is called with `process.env.CALCOM_APP_CREDENTIAL_ENCRYPTION_KEY || ""` and JSON.parse of the result, with no try/catch, so a ciphertext encrypted with a different key or any non-JSON plaintext throws inside the handler. An attacker (or misconfigured self-hoster) sends a valid secret header with garbage ciphertext and gets an unhandled 500 with a stack trace in logs, and a self-hoster with a mismatched key silently gets 500s for every sync.

[BUG] parseRefreshTokenResponse mutates `refreshTokenResponse.data`, which is a frozen zod parse result in zod 3.9+, so assigning `refresh_token` throws TypeError instead of filling the default. Any token response lacking refresh_token under zod >=3.9 crashes with 'Cannot assign to read only property' instead of completing the refresh.

[ADVISORY] When credential sync is enabled the schema validation is downgraded from the app-specific token schema (googleCredentialSchema, zoomRefreshedTokenSchema, refreshTokenResponseSchema) to a nearly unconstrained minimum schema. Self-hosters who enable sync lose all type validation of provider tokens; a subtly wrong sync response is persisted as a credential and surfaces later as mysterious per-app failures that non-sync users can never hit.

[ADVISORY] The sync-mode fetch sends calcomUserId and appSlug to CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT with no authentication header, no signature, and no secret, while the inbound webhook verifies CALCOM_WEBHOOK_SECRET. An attacker who can reach the sync endpoint (e.g. an internal service exposed by the self-hoster) can request arbitrary users' OAuth tokens for any appSlug, exfiltrating live provider credentials; the security guarantee accepted for the inbound direction was silently not mirrored outbound.

adjudication_records.primary_judge_reasoning: The candidate describes the same runtime bug: in the sync endpoint branch, refreshOAuthTokens returns a fetch Response without a `.data` property, but the caller reads `res?.data`, yielding undefined and causing `token.access_token` to throw. It also notes the mismatch in return shape between branches, aligning with the golden comment’s concern about inconsistent return types.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] In sync mode refreshOAuthTokens returns a fetch Response, but the code immediately reads `zohoCrmTokenInfo.data.error` and `zohoCrmTokenInfo.data.expiryDate`. Response has no `.data` property, so `zohoCrmTokenInfo.data.error` throws TypeError on the very first Zoho CRM token refresh when credential sync is enabled — the feature path never works for Zoho CRM.

adjudication.rationale: `refreshOAuthTokens` returns a `fetch` `Response` object when `APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED && process.env.CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT && userId` (see `packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/refreshOAuthTokens.ts`). In `packages/app-store/zohocrm/lib/CalendarService.ts`, the code wraps an Axios call with `refreshOAuthTokens(...)` and then immediately accesses `zohoCrmTokenInfo.data.error` / `zohoCrmTokenInfo.data.expiryDate`. In sync mode, `zohoCrmTokenInfo` would be a `Response` (no `.data`), causing a runtime `TypeError` and breaking Zoho CRM refresh on that path.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] The Bigin code reads `tokenInfo.data.error` / `tokenInfo.data` from the return of refreshOAuthTokens, which in sync mode is a fetch Response with no `.data`; additionally the third argument `credentialId` is passed but the surrounding code only defines `credentialKey`/`credential`-derived values, not a `credentialId` in scope. Sync mode crashes with TypeError on `.data`; and if `credentialId` is not defined in this scope the module fails TypeScript compilation outright, breaking the build for all consumers of this package.

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/app-store/zoho-bigin/lib/CalendarService.ts`, `tokenInfo` is set via `refreshOAuthTokens(...)` and then the code accesses `tokenInfo.data.error` / `tokenInfo.data` (Axios-style). But `refreshOAuthTokens` returns a `fetch(...)` Response object when `APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED && CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT && userId` is true, and a `Response` has no `.data`, so this will throw at runtime in sync mode. Also, the call passes `credentialId` as the third argument (`refreshOAuthTokens(..., "zoho-bigin", credentialId)`), but in the shown scope only `credential`/`credentialKey` are referenced; `credentialId` is not defined in the diff hunk, which would cause a TS compile error if it’s truly not declared elsewhere in the file.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] The result of refreshOAuthTokens is typed and consumed as HubspotToken (e.g. hubspotRefreshToken.refresh_token / expiry fields), but in sync mode it is a fetch Response object whose properties are body/bodyUsed/headers, not OAuth token fields. hubspotRefreshToken.refresh_token and friends are undefined in sync mode, so the HubSpot credential is persisted with undefined access token and garbage expiry, and all subsequent HubSpot API calls fail with 401.
matched_golden_ids: When APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED and CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT are set, the refreshFunction helper returns the fetch Response, but several callers (for example GoogleCalendarService.refreshAccessToken expecting res.data, and HubspotCalendarService.refreshAccessToken expecting a HubspotToken) assume it returns the integration-specific token object. That mismatch will cause runtime errors in the sync-enabled path unless the return type or those call sites are adjusted.
adjudication_records.primary_judge_reasoning: Both describe the same core bug: in the credential-sync enabled path the refresh helper returns a fetch Response object, but callers (notably HubSpot refreshAccessToken) treat the return value as an integration-specific token object, leading to undefined token fields and runtime failures. The candidate focuses on HubSpot effects, while the golden also mentions Google, but the underlying mismatch is identical.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] The new unconditional Salesforce refresh gate checks `response.statusText !== "OK"`, but statusText is a human-readable reason phrase that many clients/proxies/servers do not set (and can be localized or empty for a 200 response). A 200 response with statusText '' (e.g. behind some proxies/HTTP2 stacks where reason phrases are dropped) throws HttpError 400 even though the refresh succeeded, breaking every Salesforce calendar operation for those deployments.
matched_golden_ids: The Salesforce integration checks `response.statusText` instead of `response.ok` when handling OAuth token refresh responses. This can lead to unreliable behavior, as a successful response may not be correctly identified, resulting in the use of stale credentials and potential authentication failures.
adjudication_records.primary_judge_reasoning: Both comments identify the same underlying bug: the Salesforce OAuth refresh handler relies on `response.statusText` (e.g., comparing to "OK") rather than a reliable success indicator like `response.ok`/status code. This can misclassify successful refresh responses (empty/localized statusText), leading to incorrect error handling and downstream authentication/operation failures.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The constructor now performs a blocking remote POST to login.salesforce.com and a Prisma credential.update on every SalesforceCalendarService instantiation, where previously jsforce.Connection refreshed tokens lazily only when an access token expired. Every Salesforce calendar operation (and every booking touching Salesforce) now pays an extra OAuth round-trip plus a DB write per instantiation — a hot-path regression and a new network failure point that turns previously-cached-token operations into hard failures when Salesforce is slow or rate-limits.

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows new unconditional token refresh + DB write in `SalesforceCalendarService`: after `const credentialKey = credential.key...`, it immediately `fetch`es `https://login.salesforce.com/services/oauth2/token` and then runs `await prisma.credential.update(...)` before returning a `new jsforce.Connection(...)`. There is no check for token expiry/need-to-refresh, so every service initialization now incurs a remote OAuth round-trip and a Prisma update, adding hot-path latency and a new failure point (e.g., slow/rate-limited Salesforce). This is a concrete performance/architecture regression risk rather than a strict correctness bug.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The office365 refresh path previously logged the zod error and MS response on parse failure before continuing; parseRefreshTokenResponse throws instead, and the success/error branch and console.error were deleted, so `tokenResponse.success` is always true at the spread site while a failed parse now propagates as an unhandled generic Error('Invalid refreshed tokens were returned'). Operators debugging Office365 token refresh issues lose the MS response payload from logs; a transient malformed MS response that previously degraded gracefully now crashes the booking request with a stack trace and no diagnostic data.

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/app-store/office365calendar/lib/CalendarService.ts`, the refresh path changed from `refreshTokenResponseSchema.safeParse(responseJson)` plus a `console.error(..., responseJson)` on failure to `parseRefreshTokenResponse(responseJson, refreshTokenResponseSchema)`, which throws `new Error("Invalid refreshed tokens were returned")` without including/logging the Microsoft response payload. The old explicit logging branch was removed. This is a concrete, diff-grounded observability/regression concern (loss of diagnostic MS payload and zod error details); whether throwing is a bug is not strictly verifiable from the diff, but the loss of actionable logs is.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED is typed as `string | undefined` (the && of two env strings), not a boolean, so every `if (APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED && ...)` and the webhook's `if (!APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED)` rely on implicit truthiness of a non-empty string. If either env var is set to a whitespace or placeholder value (e.g. copied from .env.example as `""` is left but a space is pasted in), the flag silently flips on and all token refreshes route to the (broken) sync path; a boolean coercion or explicit check would fail fast instead.

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/lib/constants.ts`, `APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED` is defined as `process.env.CALCOM_WEBHOOK_SECRET && process.env.CALCOM_APP_CREDENTIAL_ENCRYPTION_KEY`, which at runtime yields the second env var string (or `undefined`), not a boolean. The diff shows it being used as a boolean gate (e.g. `if (!APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED)` in `apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts` and `if (APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED && process.env.CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT ...)` in the new OAuth helpers). This relies on implicit truthiness of non-empty strings, so mis-set values like whitespace would incorrectly enable the feature and route behavior down the “sharing/sync” paths with invalid secrets/keys instead of failing fast.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] parseRefreshTokenResponse throws a generic Error when safeParse fails, but in non-sync mode it receives full typed schemas (e.g. googleCredentialSchema) that include fields like refresh_token — so a partially-populated refresh response that previously failed only the strict parse now either passes the minimum schema (sync mode) or crashes the request with an unhandled error instead of the caller's previous graceful handling (see office365 deleted error-logging branch). Zoom and Google refresh paths that previously handled safeParse failure inline (zoom's parsedToken.success check, office365's logged-continue) now throw before that check is reachable, converting degraded-but-logged cases into 500s during booking.

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/parseRefreshTokenResponse.ts`, `parseRefreshTokenResponse` calls `schema.safeParse(...)` (or the minimum schema) and then **throws** `new Error("Invalid refreshed tokens were returned")` when `success` is false. However, multiple call sites still treat the return value like a `safeParse` result they can handle (e.g. `zoomvideo` assigns `const parsedToken = parseRefreshTokenResponse(...)` where the surrounding logic historically checked `parsedToken.success`, and `office365calendar` previously had an explicit `if (!tokenResponse.success) { console.error(...) }` branch which is now removed). Because the helper throws before returning a `{ success: false }` object, those graceful/diagnostic paths become unreachable and failures will now propagate as unhandled exceptions (likely 500s) rather than logged/handled degradation. This behavioral change is directly introduced by the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] minimumTokenResponseSchema uses computed object keys `[z.string().toString()]`, which evaluate to the literal key "ZodString" (or similar), so the schema does not allow arbitrary extra properties like refresh_token, expiry_date, or scope at all. When credential sharing is enabled, every provider refresh response is parsed against a schema requiring a property literally named "ZodString" to be a number and permitting nothing else; zod's default strips unknown keys, so parsed data contains only access_token (and drops refresh_token, expiry_date, instance_url, etc.), which callers then read as undefined — Google reads token.expiry_date as undefined and Zoho/Salesforce lose instance_url, producing broken credentials written to the DB.

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/parseRefreshTokenResponse.ts`, `minimumTokenResponseSchema` is defined with computed keys `[z.string().toString()]` and `[z.string().optional().toString()]`. In JS/TS these expressions evaluate immediately to literal strings (e.g. "ZodString"/"ZodOptional"), so the schema does **not** accept arbitrary token-response properties like `expiry_date`, `expires_in`, `scope`, `instance_url`, etc. When `APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED` and `CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT` are set, `parseRefreshTokenResponse()` uses this schema, which will either fail parsing real provider responses (throwing "Invalid refreshed tokens were returned") or not validate/retain the expected fields. This is directly introduced by the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] The function unconditionally replaces a missing refresh_token with the placeholder string "refresh_token" before the parsed result is persisted to prisma.credential by callers. In sharing mode, minimumTokenResponseSchema (see above) never yields a refresh_token, so every refresh overwrites the user's stored real refresh_token with the literal "refresh_token"; the next refresh attempt (and any fallback to the provider's real endpoint) sends "refresh_token" as the grant, permanently bricking the integration until the user re-authorizes.

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/parseRefreshTokenResponse.ts`, the helper forces `refreshTokenResponse.data.refresh_token = "refresh_token"` whenever the parsed payload lacks a refresh_token. In “sharing mode” it parses with `minimumTokenResponseSchema`, which does not include `refresh_token` and (without `.passthrough()`) will strip it even if present, so `.data.refresh_token` will always be missing and thus replaced with the literal placeholder. Callers then persist/merge this into the credential key (e.g. `packages/app-store/office365calendar/lib/CalendarService.ts` spreads `tokenResponse.data` into `o365AuthCredentials` and updates prisma), which would overwrite the real stored refresh_token with the placeholder and break subsequent refreshes until re-auth.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] In sharing mode refreshOAuthTokens returns a raw fetch Response, but the Hubspot, Zoho Bigin, Zoho CRM and Google callers expect provider-specific shapes (hubspot client object with fields, axios response with `.data`, google `{res:{data}}`). When CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT is set, hubspot's `hubspotRefreshToken.refresh_token`, zoho's `tokenInfo.data.error`, and google's `res?.data` all read undefined/throw TypeError on a fetch Response (which has no `.data`), crashing every booking that touches those integrations instead of refreshing tokens.

adjudication.rationale: In sharing mode (`APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED && process.env.CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT && userId`), `refreshOAuthTokens` returns the raw `fetch(...)` Response from `CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT` (packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/refreshOAuthTokens.ts). Multiple callers still treat the return value as a provider/axios/google client result: GoogleCalendarService does `const token = res?.data` (expects an axios-like `{data}`) (packages/app-store/googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts), Hubspot types the return as `HubspotToken` and will read token fields (packages/app-store/hubspot/lib/CalendarService.ts), and Zoho Bigin/Zoho CRM access `tokenInfo.data...` / `zohoCrmTokenInfo.data...` (expects axios response) (packages/app-store/zoho-bigin/lib/CalendarService.ts, packages/app-store/zohocrm/lib/CalendarService.ts). A fetch Response has no `.data` and does not directly expose token fields, so these paths will yield undefined and/or throw, breaking token refresh in sharing mode.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED gates the feature on only CALCOM_WEBHOOK_SECRET and CALCOM_APP_CREDENTIAL_ENCRYPTION_KEY, omitting the sibling flag CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT that refreshOAuthTokens additionally requires, leaving two inconsistent definitions of "enabled" on the same touched credential path. A self-hoster who sets the webhook secret and encryption key but not (or mis-spells) the sync endpoint gets the webhook endpoint active (accepting and overwriting credentials for any user id) while token refresh silently falls back to the provider endpoint — i.e., the feature appears enabled in one half of the path and disabled in the other, with no validation or error telling the operator which flag is missing.

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows two different “enabled” checks for the same overall credential-sync feature path. `APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED` is defined only as `process.env.CALCOM_WEBHOOK_SECRET && process.env.CALCOM_APP_CREDENTIAL_ENCRYPTION_KEY` (packages/lib/constants.ts). The new webhook endpoint `/api/webhook/app-credential` uses only that flag (plus the header secret match) to allow credential writes, and does not require `CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT`. Meanwhile `refreshOAuthTokens` additionally requires `process.env.CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT` to take the sync-path; otherwise it silently falls back to the provider refresh logic. This inconsistency is grounded in the diff and could confuse operators / lead to partially enabled behavior without validation. The claim that the webhook endpoint will accept updates for any `userId` is also true given a correct secret header, though it’s gated by the shared secret.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED is `env && env`, which evaluates to a string (or undefined), not a boolean; it is exported from a constants module full of boolean flags and consumed in boolean contexts. Consumers get a truthy string (e.g. the secret value) wherever they expect `true`; any future use in a strict boolean context (zod boolean schema, a boolean API field, `=== true` check) silently misfires, and the exported value leaks the raw secret string into anything that serializes the flag.

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/lib/constants.ts`, `APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED` is defined as `process.env.CALCOM_WEBHOOK_SECRET && process.env.CALCOM_APP_CREDENTIAL_ENCRYPTION_KEY`, which evaluates to the second env var’s *string* value (or `undefined`), not a boolean. This is exported as a "flag" and consumed as a boolean in the diff (e.g. `if (!APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED)` in `apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts`, and `if (APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED && ...)` in the new oauth helpers). That means the exported value is not `true/false` and could misbehave in strict boolean contexts (`=== true`, schemas, serialization), and it also risks propagating the raw secret string where a boolean is expected.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] The handler calls appCredentialWebhookRequestBodySchema.parse (throwing .parse, not safeParse) and has no HTTP method check, so malformed bodies and GET requests fall through to an unhandled ZodError. A caller POSTing an invalid payload (or hitting the endpoint with GET) receives a 500 from the framework's unhandled error instead of the 4xx the endpoint's own validation contract promises, and repeated bad requests generate error-alert noise indistinguishable from real failures.
matched_golden_ids: The `appCredentialWebhookRequestBodySchema.parse` function can throw on invalid payloads, resulting in 500 Internal Server Errors instead of the expected 400 Bad Request responses. This can lead to confusion for clients and hinder proper error handling.
adjudication_records.primary_judge_reasoning: The candidate flags that using Zod's `.parse` (instead of `safeParse`/handled errors) can throw on invalid payloads, resulting in an unhandled ZodError and a 500 response instead of a client-facing 400/4xx. This is the same underlying issue as the golden comment; the extra note about missing HTTP method check is additional but doesn’t change the core match.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] The webhook accepts an arbitrary userId and appSlug and overwrites that user's stored credential key with attacker-supplied decrypted JSON without any check that the key matches the app's expected credential schema. Anyone holding the single shared CALCOM_WEBHOOK_SECRET (one secret for all apps and all users, no per-caller scoping) can replace any user's app credential with arbitrary keys of the wrong shape; downstream CalendarService code then reads undefined fields from the key and every booking for that user fails, with no audit trail distinguishing webhook-written credentials from OAuth-written ones.

adjudication.rationale: In `apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts`, the handler accepts `userId` and `appSlug` from the request body and, after only checking a single shared header secret (`req.headers[CALCOM_WEBHOOK_HEADER_NAME] === CALCOM_WEBHOOK_SECRET`), decrypts `keys` and writes it directly to `prisma.credential.update/create` (`data: { key: keys }`) without validating the decrypted JSON against any app-specific credential schema. This means anyone who knows the shared webhook secret can target any `userId` and any app slug present in `appStoreMetadata` and overwrite that user’s stored credential with arbitrarily-shaped JSON, which can plausibly break downstream code that expects certain fields in `credential.key`.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The Salesforce refresh is hard-coded as an unconditional fetch to login.salesforce.com in the service constructor and is not routed through refreshOAuthTokens like every other integration in this diff, so the feature silently does not cover Salesforce. Self-hosters using credential sync get Salesforce refreshing against the provider endpoint with local app keys that may not exist on their instance (this is the exact scenario the feature exists for); additionally the network call now fires on every service construction even when the stored access token is still valid, and the `response.statusText !== "OK"` check is fragile under HTTP/2 (statusText is empty) so valid responses will be rejected with a 400.

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/app-store/salesforce/lib/CalendarService.ts`, the constructor now unconditionally performs a refresh fetch to `https://login.salesforce.com/services/oauth2/token` and updates the credential before returning a `jsforce.Connection` (see the new `const response = await fetch(...)` block right after `const credentialKey = ...`). This refresh path is not routed through the newly added `refreshOAuthTokens` helper (unlike the other integrations in this diff), so when `APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED` + `CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT` are set, Salesforce will still hit the provider token endpoint instead of the sync endpoint, undermining the feature’s intended coverage. Additionally, the error check `if (response.statusText !== "OK")` is fragile and can reject valid responses (better to use `response.ok` / `response.status`), making this a correctness bug grounded in the shown code.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] zoho-bigin passes `credentialId` to refreshOAuthTokens' `userId` parameter while every other call site passes `credential.userId`. If `credentialId` is the numeric credential id rather than the user id, the sync endpoint receives the wrong identifier (or undefined, silently disabling sync for zoho-bigin), so zoho-bigin credentials either sync under the wrong user or never sync at all — inconsistent with the sibling call sites in the same diff.

[ADVISORY] The diff removes the branch that logged zod errors on failed refresh-token parses (relying on parseRefreshTokenResponse's throw instead) but keeps persisting the credential with `tokenResponse.success && tokenResponse.data` spread, mixing a throwing helper with a non-throwing spread pattern left over from the old safeParse flow. A maintainer reading the code sees both a throw-on-failure helper and dead `success &&` guard logic; the next change here is riskier because the two failure-handling styles coexist in one function, and the diagnostic context (raw MS response) that used to be logged is now lost, making production refresh failures undiagnosable.

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/app-store/office365calendar/lib/CalendarService.ts`, the diff replaces `refreshTokenResponseSchema.safeParse(responseJson)` plus an explicit `console.error(...)` on failure with `parseRefreshTokenResponse(responseJson, refreshTokenResponseSchema)`, which throws on parse failure without logging the raw MS response. The subsequent line `o365AuthCredentials = { ...o365AuthCredentials, ...(tokenResponse.success && tokenResponse.data) }` is now redundant because `parseRefreshTokenResponse` throws when `success` is false, so `success &&` is effectively dead-guard logic left over from the old safeParse flow. This is not a functional defect, but it is a real maintainability/diagnostics regression grounded in the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The diff adds a new authenticated write API endpoint and two new shared OAuth utilities (refreshOAuthTokens, parseRefreshTokenResponse) that alter the token-refresh path of eight integrations, with zero test files or assertions anywhere in the diff (no spec/test/itest-shaped file appears in the changed paths). A regression in the placeholder refresh_token mutation or the raw-Response return type (both present in this diff) would break every booking on the affected integrations and ship undetected; there is no verification of the webhook's auth rejection, schema validation, or create-vs-update branch, and no fixture proving the sync endpoint contract (fetch body shape, response shape) matches what all eight call sites expect.

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces verifiable correctness issues beyond “missing tests”. `parseRefreshTokenResponse()` returns a Zod `safeParse` result (`{ success, data, error }`), but at least one call site treats it as the parsed credential object: in `packages/app-store/googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts`, `const key = parseRefreshTokenResponse(googleCredentials, googleCredentialSchema);` is then persisted via `prisma.credential.update({ data: { key } })`, which would store the wrapper object instead of the credential payload (previously `googleCredentialSchema.parse(...)` returned the payload). Also, `refreshOAuthTokens()` returns a raw `fetch` `Response` when sync is enabled, but some callers expect a token JSON/object (e.g. `packages/app-store/hubspot/lib/CalendarService.ts` assigns its return to `HubspotToken`), which would break at runtime when the env flags enable the sync path.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The fetch to CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT sends no authentication header, no Content-Type, and no timeout or error handling; the sync response is also a parallel hand-maintained contract with the webhook handler on the other side, with no shared schema as a single source of truth. Any operator who exposes the sync endpoint (as .env.example instructs) has an unauthenticated POST accepting calcomUserId/appSlug; and because the request/response shape exists only as comments in two files, the next edit to one side (e.g. adding the webhook secret header) drifts silently from the other, failing at runtime only during a live token refresh in a booking flow.

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/refreshOAuthTokens.ts`, when `APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED` and `CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT` are set, the code issues a `fetch(process.env.CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT, { method: "POST", body: new URLSearchParams({ calcomUserId, appSlug }) })` with no explicit auth mechanism, no explicit headers, and no error/timeout handling (it returns the raw response). The diff also shows the request/response expectations are only described via comments (here and in `apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts`) rather than a shared schema/type. While this isn’t a directly provable defect in this repo (the remote endpoint’s security/contract is external and operator-defined), it is a concrete, diff-grounded design/security robustness concern created by the change.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] minimumTokenResponseSchema uses computed keys `[z.string().toString()]` and `[z.string().optional().toString()]`, which evaluate to the literal property name `[object Object]`-style strings, making the schema require a mandatory numeric property that no real OAuth token response ever contains. When APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED and CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT are set, every safeParse fails, parseRefreshTokenResponse throws 'Invalid refreshed tokens were returned', and token refresh (and thus every calendar/video operation using those credentials) breaks for Google, Office365, Zoom, and Salesforce users.
matched_golden_ids: The Zod schema in parseRefreshTokenResponse uses computed property keys [z.string().toString()] and [z.string().optional().toString()] in minimumTokenResponseSchema, which is invalid Zod syntax and will throw a runtime error.
adjudication_records.primary_judge_reasoning: The candidate flags the same core problem: minimumTokenResponseSchema uses computed property keys like `[z.string().toString()]` and `[z.string().optional().toString()]`, which is invalid/misguided Zod object key syntax and results in incorrect schema keys (e.g., "[object Object]") causing safeParse to fail and runtime errors in parseRefreshTokenResponse.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] parseRefreshTokenResponse unconditionally (in both the credential-sharing and the default path) replaces a missing refresh_token with the literal string "refresh_token" before the parsed object is persisted as the credential key. On the default (non-sync) path for apps whose refresh responses legitimately omit refresh_token (e.g. some providers rotate only access tokens), the credential key is silently overwritten with a bogus refresh_token; the next refresh attempt sends the literal string 'refresh_token' to the provider and fails permanently — a behavior change to unrelated flows not required by the credential-sync feature.

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/parseRefreshTokenResponse.ts`, after a successful parse the code unconditionally sets `refreshTokenResponse.data.refresh_token = "refresh_token"` when it is missing. This happens regardless of whether the credential-sharing path or the default schema path is used. Call sites then use the parsed result to build/persist updated credentials (e.g. Office365: `o365AuthCredentials = { ...o365AuthCredentials, ...(tokenResponse.success && tokenResponse.data) };`), so a provider response that omits `refresh_token` can lead to the stored refresh token being overwritten with the literal string, breaking future refreshes.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] When credential sharing is enabled, full per-app schema validation (zoomRefreshedTokenSchema, refreshTokenResponseSchema, googleCredentialSchema, salesforceTokenSchema) is discarded in favor of the broken minimum schema, so garbage or malformed token payloads are accepted whenever they contain an access_token. A credential-sync endpoint returning malformed data (missing instance_url for Salesforce, expiry_date for Google, etc.) passes validation, corrupt credentials get persisted via prisma.credential.update, and subsequent API calls fail in provider-specific ways instead of being rejected at refresh time — validation weakened on the sync path with no requirement justifying it.

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds `parseRefreshTokenResponse` which, when `APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED && CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT`, ignores the passed per-app Zod schema and instead validates with `minimumTokenResponseSchema` (packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/parseRefreshTokenResponse.ts). That is a clear weakening of validation on the “credential sharing/sync enabled” path. Additionally, the “minimum” schema is itself incorrectly constructed using computed keys like `[z.string().toString()]`, so it does not actually express “any numeric expiry field” and will behave unexpectedly. This combination can let invalid/partial token shapes bypass the intended per-provider schema checks on the sharing-enabled path and then be used to update stored credentials in refresh flows.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] The Salesforce CalendarService constructor now performs an unconditional eager token refresh fetch to login.salesforce.com on every instantiation, replacing the previous jsforce-managed refresh flow; this work is not traceable to the stated 'credential sync' intent and runs even when APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED is false. Every Salesforce calendar operation now adds a blocking network round-trip (and a DB write) on the hot path even for standard self-hosted installs with no credential sharing configured; a Salesforce outage or 429 on the token endpoint now fails calendar reads/writes that previously used the cached access token via jsforce.

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/app-store/salesforce/lib/CalendarService.ts`, the constructor (or initialization path) now unconditionally performs a refresh-token `fetch("https://login.salesforce.com/services/oauth2/token", ...)` and then `prisma.credential.update(...)` before returning a `new jsforce.Connection(...)` (see the newly added block starting around `const response = await fetch(...)`). This runs regardless of `APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED` (no guard around the fetch/update), adding a blocking network round-trip and DB write on each instantiation and making all Salesforce calendar operations fail if the token endpoint is down/returns non-OK (it throws on `response.statusText !== "OK"`). Those behaviors are directly verifiable from the diff and can regress reliability/performance even when credential sharing is not configured.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] The new eager refresh checks `response.statusText !== "OK"` but Salesforce returns HTTP 200 with statusText "" (HTTP/2 has no reason phrase, and Node fetch populates statusText from the response), so non-2xx bodies are not the only failure this misses; additionally the refreshed key persisted via prisma.credential.update drops refresh_token context when accessTokenParsed comes from the broken minimum schema (no refresh_token field), storing a credential whose key lacks refresh_token unless re-added. On any Salesforce instantiation where the refresh response lacks refresh_token (always, per RFC refresh responses), the persisted key omits refresh_token except where the 'refresh_token' placeholder hack re-inserts the literal string, breaking the next refresh for all Salesforce users.

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/app-store/salesforce/lib/CalendarService.ts`, the new refresh flow checks `if (response.statusText !== "OK")` to decide failure. This is a correctness bug because `statusText` is not a reliable indicator of HTTP success (it can be empty or non-"OK" even for 2xx responses), so the code may throw on successful refreshes; it should use `response.ok`/`response.status` instead. However, the finding’s claim about dropping `refresh_token` on persistence is not supported by the diff: the update explicitly re-adds `refresh_token: credentialKey.refresh_token` when writing `key` back to Prisma, overriding any placeholder from `parseRefreshTokenResponse`.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] refreshOAuthTokens is called with `credentialId` (a credential identifier string) as the third parameter, which the function treats as the cal.com userId sent to the credential-sync endpoint. When credential sync is enabled, the sync endpoint receives a credential UUID string in the calcomUserId field instead of a numeric user id, so the parent application cannot resolve the user and Zoho Bigin token refresh fails for every Bigin user under the feature this PR claims to implement.
matched_golden_ids: The `refreshOAuthTokens` function is passed `credentialId` instead of `userId`, which breaks the credential sync functionality by causing incorrect user lookups. This issue can lead to failures in syncing user credentials, impacting user experience.
adjudication_records.primary_judge_reasoning: The candidate issue describes the same parameter mix-up: `refreshOAuthTokens` is being called with a `credentialId` where the function expects a Cal.com `userId`, causing the credential-sync endpoint to receive the wrong identifier and fail user lookup/sync. This matches the golden comment’s underlying bug and impact.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] The sync branch returns the raw `fetch` Response whose body is whatever the credential-sync endpoint produces (documented as 'only the access token and expiry date'), but every call site (Lark, Zoom, Webex, Office365, Zoho) immediately consumes the response with provider-specific parsing/handleErrors helpers, and the Google call site reads `res?.data` off the Response object. In sync mode Google Calendar reads `token.access_token` from a fetch Response (undefined) and assigns undefined into googleCredentials, and provider-specific error handlers run against the sync endpoint's payload shape; the 'app integration enhancement' path is untested against any of the actual consuming code and diverges from every call site's expected contract.

adjudication.rationale: In sync mode (`APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED && CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT && userId`), `refreshOAuthTokens` returns the raw Fetch API `Response` from `fetch(process.env.CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT, ...)` (packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/refreshOAuthTokens.ts). Several call sites assume the returned value matches their provider refresh function’s return type/shape. This is directly broken for Google Calendar: it does `const res = await refreshOAuthTokens(...); const token = res?.data;` (packages/app-store/googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts), but a `Response` has no `.data`, so `token` becomes `undefined` and `googleCredentials.access_token` / `expiry_date` are set to `undefined`. Other integrations (e.g., Office365/Zoom/Webex/Lark) pass that `Response` into provider-specific handlers (`handleErrorsJson`, `handleZoomResponse`, `handleWebexResponse`, `handleLarkError`) which expect the provider’s payload semantics; the diff shows no adaptation layer converting the sync endpoint response into those expected shapes.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The webhook handler is scoped to accept updates for any userId and any app slug with only a shared-secret check; no per-app or per-user authorization, no HTTP method check, and string equality on the secret instead of constant-time comparison. Anyone who obtains the single shared CALCOM_WEBHOOK_SECRET (which is also used, per .env.example, for the parent application) can overwrite any user's stored OAuth credentials for any app, silently swapping calendar/video credentials; operators enabling the feature expose a credential-overwrite primitive with no audit trail.

adjudication.rationale: The newly added webhook endpoint `apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts` allows the caller to supply arbitrary `userId` and `appSlug` and will `update`/`create` credentials for that user/app after only checking a single shared secret header (no per-user/per-app authorization and no ownership checks beyond `user exists` / `app exists`). It also does not restrict HTTP method (no `req.method` guard) and compares the provided secret with `!==` directly (`req.headers[...] !== process.env.CALCOM_WEBHOOK_SECRET`), not using a constant-time comparison. This means anyone with the shared `CALCOM_WEBHOOK_SECRET` can overwrite any user’s stored credentials for any app supported by `appStoreMetadata`, which is a concrete credential-overwrite security vulnerability introduced by this diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The keys payload is decrypted with `process.env.CALCOM_APP_CREDENTIAL_ENCRYPTION_KEY || ""` and the result is JSON.parse'd with no try/catch and no schema validation of the decrypted key object before persisting it as the credential key. A request with a valid secret but malformed ciphertext (or an unset encryption key, which APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED only weakly guards via string-truthiness) causes symmetricDecrypt/JSON.parse to throw, returning a 500 and writing no useful log, and if it does parse it persists an arbitrary JSON blob as a credential key that downstream services will fail to cast.

adjudication.rationale: In the new webhook handler `apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts`, the decrypted payload is processed as `JSON.parse(symmetricDecrypt(reqBody.keys, process.env.CALCOM_APP_CREDENTIAL_ENCRYPTION_KEY || ""))` with no try/catch and no schema validation of the resulting object before persisting it (`data: { key: keys }`). Since `reqBody.keys` is only validated as a string by zod, a request with a correct webhook secret but malformed ciphertext (or any decrypt/parse failure) will throw and yield an unhandled 500. Even if parsing succeeds, it can store an arbitrary JSON object into `credential.key`, potentially breaking downstream code that assumes a specific credential shape.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The credential-sync branch does not send the refresh token or any per-app OAuth context (only calcomUserId and appSlug) to the sync endpoint, so the contract relies entirely on the parent application holding the actual OAuth client secret and refresh token — yet the webhook handler in this same PR persists key objects created from this flow. Two hand-maintained halves of a protocol (the sync fetch body and the app-credential webhook payload) evolve independently with no shared schema; a self-hoster implementing the documented endpoint must guess the response shape, and any mismatch is only discovered as runtime failures in provider-specific code paths.

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows the sync endpoint call in `packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/refreshOAuthTokens.ts` sends only `calcomUserId` and `appSlug` (no refresh token or other OAuth context), explicitly relying on the external application to manage secrets/tokens. Separately, the new webhook handler `apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts` persists decrypted `keys` into `prisma.credential`, and the runtime parsing behavior changes via `parseRefreshTokenResponse` (switching to a minimal schema when `APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED` and `CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT` are set). There is no shared/request/response schema tying the sync endpoint contract to the webhook payload contract, so mismatches would surface only at runtime in provider-specific refresh flows—this is a concrete protocol/architecture concern grounded in the added code, but not a directly provable functional defect from the diff alone.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The redirect URI is changed from `appConfig.slug` to the hardcoded literal "zoho-bigin", an unrelated behavioral edit smuggled into an import-path refactor. If appConfig.slug ever diverges from the hardcoded string (or this handler is reused for a differently-slugged deployment), the OAuth redirect URI silently mismatches the registered callback and Zoho Bigin installs break; the change is not traceable to the credential-sync requirement and should be reverted or justified in the PR description.

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/app-store/zoho-bigin/api/add.ts`, the redirect URI is changed from `WEBAPP_URL + `/api/integrations/${appConfig.slug}/callback`` to the hardcoded `WEBAPP_URL + `/api/integrations/zoho-bigin/callback``. This is a concrete behavioral change embedded among import-path refactors. The diff does not show `config.json`, so we cannot verify whether `appConfig.slug` is always `"zoho-bigin"`; if it ever differs, this would break OAuth callback matching. Even if currently equivalent, hardcoding reduces configurability and should be justified.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The diff removes the existing console.error diagnostics for zod validation failures of the refreshed Office365 token, replacing them with the shared parseRefreshTokenResponse which throws a bare 'Invalid refreshed tokens were returned' Error. Office365 operators debugging expired/malformed Microsoft token responses lose the zodError details and the raw MS response from logs, making refresh failures in production significantly harder to diagnose on both the sync and non-sync paths.
