adjudication.rationale: In `packages/app-store/office365calendar/lib/CalendarService.ts`, the prior logic did `refreshTokenResponseSchema.safeParse(responseJson)` and, on failure, logged `console.error("Outlook error grabbing new tokens ~ zodError:", tokenResponse.error, "MS response:", responseJson)`. The diff replaces this with `parseRefreshTokenResponse(responseJson, refreshTokenResponseSchema)`, whose implementation throws `new Error("Invalid refreshed tokens were returned")` on parse failure and does not log the Zod error or raw Microsoft response. This is a verifiable reduction in diagnosability/observability for token refresh failures (both sync and non-sync paths), but not necessarily a functional defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] HubSpot and Lark call sites route their refresh through refreshOAuthTokens but do not apply parseRefreshTokenResponse, while Google, Zoom, Office365 and Salesforce do — the refactor's coverage is inconsistent across apps for the same stated feature. In sync mode HubSpot/Lark receive whatever shape the sync endpoint returns with no validation at all (minimum or otherwise), so a misconfigured sync endpoint corrupts HubSpot/Lark credentials silently while the same misconfiguration is caught (loudly) for the other apps; the next maintainer must reverse-engineer which apps got which half of the feature.

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows `refreshOAuthTokens` returns a raw `fetch(...)` `Response` when sync mode is enabled (APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED && CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT && userId). Several call sites were adapted to expect a `Response` (e.g., Google uses `fetchTokens.res`, Office365 uses `handleErrorsJson(response)`, Lark passes the result to `handleLarkError(resp, ...)`). However HubSpot’s refresh path assigns the return value to a `HubspotToken` (`const hubspotRefreshToken: HubspotToken = await refreshOAuthTokens(...)`) and does not parse/validate it; in sync mode this will actually be a `Response`, not a token object, leading to broken refresh handling and/or bad credential updates. Additionally, unlike Google/Zoom/Office365/Salesforce, HubSpot and Lark do not apply `parseRefreshTokenResponse` (or any schema validation) to whatever the sync endpoint returns, making the feature’s behavior inconsistent across apps and allowing malformed payloads through for those apps.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED is derived as the string-truthy AND of CALCOM_WEBHOOK_SECRET and CALCOM_APP_CREDENTIAL_ENCRYPTION_KEY but excludes CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT, and an empty-string env var (the .env.example default) is falsy while a whitespace value silently enables the feature. Operators setting only the sync endpoint and webhook secret (per a partial reading of the .env.example block) get no sync and no warning, while a stray non-empty placeholder value in one of the two keys flips refresh behavior for every OAuth app in the instance, including replacing schema validation with the broken minimum schema — a feature toggle hidden behind two unrelated env vars with no explicit enable switch.

adjudication.rationale: The diff defines `APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED` as `process.env.CALCOM_WEBHOOK_SECRET && process.env.CALCOM_APP_CREDENTIAL_ENCRYPTION_KEY` (packages/lib/constants.ts), which is a string/undefined truthiness gate rather than an explicit boolean toggle and it indeed ignores `CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT`. Multiple call sites then branch behavior based on this flag plus the endpoint (e.g. `refreshOAuthTokens` and `parseRefreshTokenResponse` check `APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED && process.env.CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT`), so partial configuration (endpoint + webhook secret but no encryption key) will silently disable sync. Also, because env vars are strings, any non-empty/whitespace value will enable the flag. This is a real, diff-grounded configuration/feature-toggle design concern, though it’s not a directly verifiable correctness defect absent a specific misconfiguration scenario.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] The computed-key schema produces only the literal key "[object Object]" (both `z.string().toString()` and `z.string().optional().toString()` evaluate to the same string, and the second overwrites the first), so minimumTokenResponseSchema accepts only {access_token} and the comment's 'any property with a number is the expiry' is not implemented. When credential-sharing is enabled, every refreshed-token payload parsed by this schema is stripped to {access_token} (Zod strips unknown keys), so expiry and all other token fields are silently dropped, and callers persist a near-empty credential to the DB.

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/parseRefreshTokenResponse.ts`, `minimumTokenResponseSchema` uses computed keys `[z.string().toString()]` and `[z.string().optional().toString()]`. These evaluate to a single fixed string key (not a wildcard), and since both expressions produce the same key, the second definition overwrites the first in the object literal. As a result, the schema does not implement “any property with a number is the expiry” and will only reliably parse/retain `access_token` (and possibly that one literal key), while Zod’s default object behavior strips unknown keys. When credential sharing is enabled, callers using `parseRefreshTokenResponse` will therefore drop `expiry_date`/`expires_in` and other token fields from parsed data, matching the finding’s described behavior.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] Because the minimum schema never captures refresh_token (unknown keys are stripped), `refreshTokenResponse.data.refresh_token` is always undefined and the code unconditionally overwrites it with the sentinel string "refresh_token". In Google CalendarService.ts (line ~99) this stripped object is persisted as the credential key via prisma.credential.update, permanently destroying the user's real refresh_token and all other credential fields; the OAuth credential can never be refreshed again and the integration is bricked for that user.

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces `parseRefreshTokenResponse` which, when `APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED && CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT` is true, validates via `minimumTokenResponseSchema` (which does not include `refresh_token` and is not `.passthrough()`, so Zod will strip unknown keys). The function then executes `if (!refreshTokenResponse.data.refresh_token) { refreshTokenResponse.data.refresh_token = "refresh_token"; }`, guaranteeing a sentinel refresh token in that branch. In `packages/app-store/googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts`, the result of `parseRefreshTokenResponse(...)` is assigned to `key` and persisted directly via `prisma.credential.update({ data: { key } })`, so the stored credential key will not contain the original refresh token (and may only contain the minimal parsed fields plus the sentinel). This is a verifiable data-loss/bricking risk introduced by the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] The code reads `const token = res?.data` but in credential-sharing mode refreshOAuthTokens returns a raw fetch Response, which has no `data` property, so token is undefined and `token.access_token` throws TypeError. Every Google Calendar token refresh on a credential-sharing deployment crashes before persisting, taking down booking calendar operations with an unhandled TypeError instead of refreshing the token.

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/refreshOAuthTokens.ts`, credential-sharing mode returns the raw `fetch(...)` `Response` object. But `packages/app-store/googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts` still treats the return value like an axios/gaxios-style object and does `const token = res?.data;` followed by `token.access_token`/`token.expiry_date`. A `Response` has no `.data`, so `token` becomes `undefined` and `token.access_token` will throw a `TypeError` at runtime when credential sharing is enabled.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] refreshOAuthTokens is called with `credentialId` instead of `credential.userId` (confusable pair: both numbers in scope, wrong one bound), so the sync endpoint receives a credential ID where its contract (calcomUserId) specifies a user ID. When credential-sharing is enabled, the parent application looks up the wrong entity by credential-id-as-user-id, returning the wrong user's tokens or a 404, silently corrupting Bigin credential refresh.

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/app-store/zoho-bigin/lib/CalendarService.ts`, `refreshOAuthTokens` is invoked with `credentialId` as the third argument: `refreshOAuthTokens(..., "zoho-bigin", credentialId)`. The helper `refreshOAuthTokens` is defined to take `userId: number | null` and, when credential sharing is enabled, posts `{ calcomUserId: userId.toString(), appSlug }` to `CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT`. Throughout the diff, other integrations pass `credential.userId` (e.g., Hubspot/Lark/Zoom). Passing a variable named `credentialId` here is very likely a mixup that would send the credential record ID as `calcomUserId`, causing lookups against the wrong entity at the sync endpoint.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] In sharing mode refreshOAuthTokens returns a raw fetch Response, but the code types the result as HubspotToken and later accesses properties of the hubspotClient's token object (e.g. .refresh_token, .expires_in) directly on it. In sharing mode the Hubspot refresh path reads undefined properties off a Response object, producing NaN expiry and a broken credential instead of a refreshed token — the integration shape (axios-like client result vs fetch Response) is not representable by the shared return type.

adjudication.rationale: `refreshOAuthTokens` returns a `fetch` `Response` when `APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED && process.env.CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT && userId` (packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/refreshOAuthTokens.ts). In Hubspot’s `CalendarService`, the result of `await refreshOAuthTokens(...)` is typed as `HubspotToken` (packages/app-store/hubspot/lib/CalendarService.ts), but in sharing mode it will actually be a `Response`, not the Hubspot SDK token object. Any subsequent logic that expects token fields (implied by the comment about setting expiry) will read undefined properties and break refresh/update behavior.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] In sharing mode refreshOAuthTokens returns a fetch Response while the surrounding code treats the result as an axios response and reads `tokenInfo.data`, which is undefined on a Response. Bigin token refresh in sharing mode crashes on `tokenInfo.data.error`/`tokenInfo.data.access_token` access (undefined), so Bigin calendar operations fail on every shared deployment.

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/refreshOAuthTokens.ts`, when `APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED && process.env.CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT && userId` is true, the function calls `fetch(...)` and returns the raw `Response`. In `packages/app-store/zoho-bigin/lib/CalendarService.ts`, token refresh was changed to `const tokenInfo = await refreshOAuthTokens(...)` and the subsequent code still treats it like an Axios response (`tokenInfo.data.error`, and later accesses like `tokenInfo.data.access_token`). A Fetch `Response` has no `.data` property, so in sharing mode this will be `undefined` and will throw/crash when dereferenced, breaking Bigin token refresh.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] The webhook writes the decrypted keys object to `credential.key` in plaintext, while every read path decrypts credential.key with CALENDSO_ENCRYPTION_KEY (the app credential readers in app-store call symmetricDecrypt on credential.key), so synced credentials and locally-created credentials have incompatible encodings stored in the same column. Any credential created or updated via this sync webhook fails to decrypt in the consuming app services, so the synced integration is unusable; the data model has two formats in one column with no discriminator.

adjudication.rationale: In the added webhook (`apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts`), the incoming `keys` payload is decrypted with `CALCOM_APP_CREDENTIAL_ENCRYPTION_KEY` and then the resulting object is stored directly into `prisma.credential.{create,update}({ data: { key: keys }})`. However, nothing in this diff shows that "every read path decrypts credential.key with CALENDSO_ENCRYPTION_KEY" or that app-store consumers call `symmetricDecrypt(credential.key, ...)`. The app-store service changes shown continue to treat `credential.key` as a parsed object (e.g., Google/Office365/Zoom use zod schemas on the object) and do not decrypt it. Therefore the asserted incompatible encodings / guaranteed failure to decrypt cannot be verified from this diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] The constructor path now performs an unconditional token refresh POST to login.salesforce.com on every service instantiation, even when credential-sharing is disabled and the existing token is still valid, and stores `key` as the parsed minimal/salesforceTokenSchema result merged only with refresh_token — dropping any fields not in salesforceTokenSchema (e.g. expiry tracking fields) that previously lived in credential.key. Every Salesforce calendar/video operation now pays a blocking remote OAuth round-trip (hot-path regression: jsforce previously refreshed lazily on 401), and in sharing mode parseRefreshTokenResponse strips the response to {access_token}, so the persisted key loses instance_url/signature/id that jsforce needs — the connection becomes unusable on the next invocation.

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/app-store/salesforce/lib/CalendarService.ts`, the service instantiation now immediately performs a refresh-token POST to `https://login.salesforce.com/services/oauth2/token` (no conditional on expiry/need), before returning the `jsforce.Connection` (the fetch+parse+`prisma.credential.update` block added right after `const credentialKey = ...`). This makes every instantiation pay a blocking network round-trip. Also, the refreshed credential is persisted by overwriting `key` with `{ ...accessTokenParsed.data, refresh_token: credentialKey.refresh_token }`, which necessarily drops any existing fields not present in the parsed result. In credential-sharing mode, `parseRefreshTokenResponse` ignores the provided `salesforceTokenSchema` and instead parses with `minimumTokenResponseSchema` (because `APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED && CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT`), and Zod objects strip unknown keys by default—so fields like `instance_url`, `signature`, `id`, etc. from the Salesforce response would be removed and not persisted, potentially breaking subsequent uses that rely on them.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] In sharing mode parseRefreshTokenResponse parses responseBody with the broken minimum schema, so parsedToken.data contains only {access_token, refresh_token:"refresh_token"} and the Zoom credential update persists that garbage. The real Zoom refresh_token is overwritten with the literal string "refresh_token", permanently breaking token refresh for Zoom on credential-sharing deployments.

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces `parseRefreshTokenResponse()` which, in sharing mode (`APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED && CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT`), validates with `minimumTokenResponseSchema`. That schema only declares `access_token` plus two computed keys (`[z.string().toString()]`, etc.) rather than using `.catchall(...)`, so it will not preserve `refresh_token` (Zod object schemas strip unknown keys by default). The function then explicitly sets a missing `refresh_token` to the literal string `"refresh_token"`. In Zoom’s refresh flow, the code now uses `parseRefreshTokenResponse(responseBody, zoomRefreshedTokenSchema)`, so under sharing mode the parsed token result will lose the real `refresh_token` and replace it with `"refresh_token"`, which would break subsequent refreshes if that parsed data is persisted as the credential key (as typical in these adapters).

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] The shared-path fetch has no timeout, no response.ok check, no error handling, and returns a raw Response regardless of what each caller's non-shared path returns (fetch Response, axios response, hubspot client object), with the sharing gate duplicated as a raw env-var check (process.env.CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT) at every call site with no single flag constant. A slow or failed credential-sync endpoint cascades into every calendar/video refresh with an unbounded hang (no degradation), and any caller whose native library returns a non-fetch shape (Hubspot, Zoho Bigin/CRM axios) reads undefined fields — a shared-dependency failure takes down all synced integrations simultaneously.

adjudication.rationale: In the new shared refresh path, `packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/refreshOAuthTokens.ts` returns the raw `fetch()` `Response` from `CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT` with no `response.ok` check, no timeout/abort, and no try/catch. Several callers assume the non-shared return shape and will break under the shared path: e.g. Google Calendar expects a gaxios-like `{ data }` and does `const token = res?.data` (`packages/app-store/googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts`), HubSpot expects a `HubspotToken` object (`packages/app-store/hubspot/lib/CalendarService.ts`), and Zoho (axios) callers use `.data` (`packages/app-store/zoho-bigin/lib/CalendarService.ts`, `packages/app-store/zohocrm/lib/CalendarService.ts`). When the shared path is used, those will read undefined fields / fail at runtime, and a slow sync endpoint can hang token refreshes indefinitely. (One sub-claim in the finding is off: the sharing gate is centralized in `refreshOAuthTokens`/`parseRefreshTokenResponse`, not duplicated at each call site.)

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] The webhook secret comparison reads req.headers[process.env.CALCOM_WEBHOOK_HEADER_NAME] with no case normalization of the configured header name; Node lowercases header keys, so any operator who sets CALCOM_WEBHOOK_HEADER_NAME with uppercase letters (the .env.example only says 'Should be in lowercase' in a comment) gets a header lookup that never matches. The webhook returns 403 for every legitimate sync request when the env var contains uppercase characters, silently disabling credential sync with no error surfaced beyond a forbidden response.

adjudication.rationale: In `apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts`, the secret check uses `req.headers[process.env.CALCOM_WEBHOOK_HEADER_NAME || "calcom-webhook-secret"]`. Node/Next request header keys are normalized to lowercase, so if `CALCOM_WEBHOOK_HEADER_NAME` is configured with any uppercase characters, this lookup will miss and the comparison will fail, returning 403 for valid requests. The diff only documents “should be in lowercase” in `.env.example` but does not enforce normalization in code.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] refreshOAuthTokens is passed the appSlug "msteams" but the corresponding office365calendar service uses "office365-calendar" while both use the same parent-application credential store, creating two slugs for what the parent app must treat as one Microsoft integration with one set of app keys. A parent application syncing Microsoft credentials sees the same user's Microsoft credential under two different slugs, so syncing 'office365-calendar' does not cover the msteams video path and vice versa — MS Teams video calls fail to refresh in sharing mode.

adjudication.rationale: The diff does show `refreshOAuthTokens(..., "office365-calendar", ...)` in `packages/app-store/office365calendar/lib/CalendarService.ts` and `refreshOAuthTokens(..., "msteams", ...)` in `packages/app-store/office365video/lib/VideoApiAdapter.ts`. However, nothing in the diff establishes that these two paths are supposed to share the same `appSlug` for syncing, or that they are the “same parent-application credential store” that must be treated as one integration. They appear to be two distinct app-store apps (calendar vs video) with potentially different OAuth configs/scopes, and the alleged failure depends on external parent-app behavior not shown in the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The function name and parameter promise schema-pluggability but in sharing mode the caller-provided schema is discarded entirely (minimumTokenResponseSchema wins), a parallel hidden branch that contradicts the signature contract `parseRefreshTokenResponse(response, schema)`. The next developer adding expiry/refresh_token validation to a per-app schema will see their validation silently ignored on shared deployments, and failures that the schema would have caught (missing expiry) pass green while the stored credential is unusable — a stand-in guard that goes green while the real contract is broken.

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/parseRefreshTokenResponse.ts`, `parseRefreshTokenResponse(response, schema)` conditionally ignores the caller-provided `schema` when `APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED && process.env.CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT` is true, and instead validates only against `minimumTokenResponseSchema`. This is a real, diff-grounded “hidden branch” that makes the `schema` parameter ineffective in sharing mode and can surprise future callers expecting their per-app schema to be enforced.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] The minimumTokenResponseSchema uses computed keys `[z.string().toString()]` and `[z.string().optional().toString()]`, which evaluate to literal property names "z.string()"/"z.string().optional()" rather than validating arbitrary token fields, so the schema only enforces access_token and validates nothing else. When APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED, any provider response — including malformed ones missing refresh_token, expiry, or with wrong types — passes validation, and garbage credentials get persisted to the DB.

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/parseRefreshTokenResponse.ts`, `minimumTokenResponseSchema` defines computed keys as `[z.string().toString()]` and `[z.string().optional().toString()]`. Those expressions evaluate to a *single literal string key* (whatever `toString()` returns for the Zod type), not “any string key”, so the schema does not validate arbitrary token fields as intended. This is a real defect in the diff: when `APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED` is true, the safeParse will validate against an incorrect object shape (likely failing unless the response happens to contain that literal key), breaking token refresh/handling logic. The finding’s exact claim that “any provider response passes validation” isn’t accurate (it more likely fails), but the core issue—computed keys don’t do what’s intended and the schema is wrong—is verifiable.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] When the parsed data lacks refresh_token, the code assigns the literal string "refresh_token" as the refresh token (`refreshTokenResponse.data.refresh_token = "refresh_token"`). Google Calendar, Office365 and Zoom persist the literal string "refresh_token" into prisma.credential, permanently destroying the user's real refresh token; the next access-token expiry makes the integration unrecoverable without re-auth.

[BUG] refreshOAuthTokens in sync mode returns a raw fetch Response from CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT, but this call site assigns it to `hubspotRefreshToken: HubspotToken` and then reads `.expires_in`/`.refresh_token` off it, which are undefined on a Response object. With credential sync enabled, every HubSpot token refresh computes NaN expiry and writes a corrupt credential key, breaking the integration.

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/refreshOAuthTokens.ts`, when sync mode is enabled (`APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED && process.env.CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT && userId`), the function does `fetch(...)` and returns the raw `Response` object. In `packages/app-store/hubspot/lib/CalendarService.ts`, the result is typed/used as `HubspotToken` (`const hubspotRefreshToken: HubspotToken = await refreshOAuthTokens(...)`). With sync enabled, that variable will actually be a `Response`, so token fields like `.expires_in` / `.refresh_token` (used later in the refresh flow) will be undefined, leading to incorrect expiry calculations and corrupted credential updates. The mismatch is directly introduced by this diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] In sync mode refreshOAuthTokens returns a raw fetch Response, but the code does `const token = res?.data` expecting the google-auth-library result shape (`.res.data`), so `token` is undefined and `token.access_token` throws TypeError. With credential sync enabled, every Google Calendar access-token refresh crashes on `token.access_token`, breaking calendar operations entirely.

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/app-store/googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts`, `refreshAccessToken` now calls `refreshOAuthTokens(...)` and then does `const token = res?.data;` followed by `token.access_token`/`token.expiry_date`. But in sync mode (`APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED && CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT && userId`), `refreshOAuthTokens` returns the raw `fetch(...)` `Response` object (see `packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/refreshOAuthTokens.ts`), which does not have a `.data` property. That makes `token` undefined and `token.access_token` will throw at runtime, breaking refresh flow when sync mode is enabled.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] The custom sync endpoint fetch has no Authorization header or webhook secret and returns a raw Response object that every call site then consumes as the provider-specific token shape (axios response, google res object, provider JSON), a contract no call site was written for. The sync-enabled code path is non-functional for Lark, Office365, Office365 Video, Webex, Zoom and Zoho adapters as well; consumers call provider-specific handlers (handleZoomResponse, handleLarkError) or read `.data`/`.expires_in` on a plain Response.

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces `refreshOAuthTokens()` which, in the sync-enabled path, always does `fetch(process.env.CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT, ...)` and returns the raw `Response` object (no `.json()`), with no auth/secret headers (packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/refreshOAuthTokens.ts). Several call sites still assume provider/library-specific return shapes: Google expects `res.data` (googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts: `const token = res?.data;`), Hubspot expects a `HubspotToken` object with fields like `expires_in` (hubspot/lib/CalendarService.ts assigns the return to `HubspotToken`), and Zoho adapters expect an Axios response with `.data` (zohocrm/lib/CalendarService.ts, zoho-bigin/lib/CalendarService.ts). In sync mode these will receive a Fetch `Response`, so `.data`/token fields won’t exist and the code path will break. (Some other adapters already operate on `Response` from `fetch`, so the finding’s full list is overstated, but the defect is real and diff-verifiable for at least these integrations.)

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] refreshOAuthTokens is called with `credentialId` as the third argument, but the function signature is `userId: number | null` and the sync path sends it as `calcomUserId` in the POST body. With credential sync enabled, the parent application receives a credential ID as calcomUserId, so it either fails the user lookup or syncs tokens to the wrong user.

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/refreshOAuthTokens.ts`, the third parameter is `userId: number | null` and, on the sync path, it is sent as `calcomUserId` in the POST body. Most call sites pass `credential.userId`, but `packages/app-store/zoho-bigin/lib/CalendarService.ts` calls `refreshOAuthTokens(..., "zoho-bigin", credentialId)`, which (by name and contrast with other call sites) appears to be a credential identifier rather than the Cal.com user ID. If credential sync is enabled, this would POST the wrong value as `calcomUserId`, causing the parent app to look up the wrong user or fail.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] The constructor now unconditionally POSTs to login.salesforce.com/services/oauth2/token to refresh tokens on every instantiation of SalesforceCalendarService, replacing jsforce's on-demand refresh-on-401 behavior, and overwrites the stored credential key on every call. Every Salesforce calendar operation (including reads with a valid unexpired access token) makes an extra network round-trip to Salesforce, and concurrent calls race to overwrite the credential row; if Salesforce rate-limits or the refresh fails, previously-working calendar access now fails.

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/app-store/salesforce/lib/CalendarService.ts`, the service now performs an `await fetch("https://login.salesforce.com/services/oauth2/token", ...)` refresh flow unconditionally before returning the `jsforce.Connection`, and then immediately updates the credential row via `prisma.credential.update(...)`. This means every instantiation triggers an extra network call and can fail calendar operations if the refresh request is rate-limited/errored even when an existing access token might still be usable. The unconditional write also introduces a race when multiple instances run concurrently, repeatedly overwriting the same credential row.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] parseRefreshTokenResponse throws `new Error("Invalid refreshed tokens were returned")` on parse failure, replacing the previous behavior which logged the zod error and MS response and continued with `tokenResponse.success && tokenResponse.data`. Office365 token responses that previously degraded gracefully (logged, keys updated with whatever parsed) now abort the whole refreshAccessToken with an unhandled error, breaking booking flows that previously succeeded.

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/parseRefreshTokenResponse.ts`, `parseRefreshTokenResponse` now does `schema.safeParse(...)` (or `minimumTokenResponseSchema.safeParse(...)`) and immediately `throw new Error("Invalid refreshed tokens were returned")` when `!refreshTokenResponse.success`. In `packages/app-store/office365calendar/lib/CalendarService.ts`, this replaces the prior behavior where `refreshTokenResponseSchema.safeParse(responseJson)` could fail, the code would `console.error(...)`, and then continue by spreading only `(tokenResponse.success && tokenResponse.data)` into `o365AuthCredentials` (i.e., not throwing). With the new helper, any schema mismatch will abort `refreshAccessToken` via an exception, and there is no local try/catch in the shown code path, so this is a real behavior change that can surface as a runtime failure where it previously continued.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] symmetricDecrypt is called with `process.env.CALCOM_APP_CREDENTIAL_ENCRYPTION_KEY || ""` and JSON.parse of the result, with no try/catch, so a ciphertext encrypted with a different key or any non-JSON plaintext throws inside the handler. An attacker (or misconfigured self-hoster) sends a valid secret header with garbage ciphertext and gets an unhandled 500 with a stack trace in logs, and a self-hoster with a mismatched key silently gets 500s for every sync.

adjudication.rationale: In `apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts`, the handler does `JSON.parse(symmetricDecrypt(reqBody.keys, process.env.CALCOM_APP_CREDENTIAL_ENCRYPTION_KEY || ""))` with no error handling. While `APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED` implies the env key is set (so the `|| ""` is likely unused), a bad/mismatched ciphertext (or non-JSON plaintext after decrypt) will throw during decrypt and/or `JSON.parse`, bubbling up as an unhandled exception and producing a 500 response instead of a controlled 4xx. This matches the finding’s claim about misconfigurations or bad payloads causing 500s.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] parseRefreshTokenResponse mutates `refreshTokenResponse.data`, which is a frozen zod parse result in zod 3.9+, so assigning `refresh_token` throws TypeError instead of filling the default. Any token response lacking refresh_token under zod >=3.9 crashes with 'Cannot assign to read only property' instead of completing the refresh.

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows `parseRefreshTokenResponse` does mutate `refreshTokenResponse.data.refresh_token` after a successful `safeParse`, but the claim that Zod’s `safeParse` result/data is "frozen" in Zod 3.9+ (and would therefore throw a `TypeError` on assignment) is not something that can be verified from this PR diff. There’s no evidence in the diff of any freezing/immutability behavior being enabled, and Zod’s runtime freezing is not established here. So the specific crash scenario asserted by the finding is not verifiable from the diff alone.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] When credential sync is enabled the schema validation is downgraded from the app-specific token schema (googleCredentialSchema, zoomRefreshedTokenSchema, refreshTokenResponseSchema) to a nearly unconstrained minimum schema. Self-hosters who enable sync lose all type validation of provider tokens; a subtly wrong sync response is persisted as a credential and surfaces later as mysterious per-app failures that non-sync users can never hit.

adjudication.rationale: The diff explicitly changes validation behavior when sync is enabled: `parseRefreshTokenResponse()` selects `minimumTokenResponseSchema.safeParse(response)` instead of the app-specific `schema.safeParse(response)` when `APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED && process.env.CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT` (packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/parseRefreshTokenResponse.ts). Call sites for Google/Office365/Zoom/etc were updated to use this helper, so enabling sync does bypass the stricter provider schemas and accept a much looser shape before updating credentials. This is a concrete, diff-grounded robustness/maintainability concern (bad sync responses can pass validation and be persisted), though it’s also plausibly an intentional tradeoff for self-host sync flexibility rather than a guaranteed defect in all environments.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The sync-mode fetch sends calcomUserId and appSlug to CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT with no authentication header, no signature, and no secret, while the inbound webhook verifies CALCOM_WEBHOOK_SECRET. An attacker who can reach the sync endpoint (e.g. an internal service exposed by the self-hoster) can request arbitrary users' OAuth tokens for any appSlug, exfiltrating live provider credentials; the security guarantee accepted for the inbound direction was silently not mirrored outbound.

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds `refreshOAuthTokens` which, when `APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED` and `CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT` are set, POSTs to `process.env.CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT` with only `calcomUserId` and `appSlug` in the body and no auth header/signature/secret (`packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/refreshOAuthTokens.ts`). In contrast, the inbound webhook handler explicitly verifies a shared secret in a configurable header (`apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts` using `CALCOM_WEBHOOK_SECRET`/`CALCOM_WEBHOOK_HEADER_NAME`). The finding that outbound requests are not authenticated (and thus the security model is asymmetric) is directly supported by the diff and is a security defect in the added sync mode.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED is a raw string concatenation of two env values (`process.env.CALCOM_WEBHOOK_SECRET && process.env.CALCOM_APP_CREDENTIAL_ENCRYPTION_KEY`), so the constant is the value of the secret rather than a boolean, and is enabled solely by setting two env vars with no feature flag. Operators who set CALCOM_WEBHOOK_SECRET for any other purpose (it is a generically-named webhook secret) silently activate credential sync, redirecting all OAuth refreshes to CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT when set — behavior cannot be toggled independently of the secret and leaks the secret's value into any place the 'boolean' is serialized.

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/lib/constants.ts`, `APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED` is defined as `process.env.CALCOM_WEBHOOK_SECRET && process.env.CALCOM_APP_CREDENTIAL_ENCRYPTION_KEY`, which in JS/TS evaluates to the *second env var’s string value* (or `undefined`), not a boolean. The diff shows this value being used as a flag (`if (!APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED)` and `if (APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED && process.env.CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT ...)`). That works via truthiness, but it’s easy to misuse later (e.g., serialize/log the exported constant and inadvertently expose the encryption key). The claim that this “redirects all OAuth refreshes” is slightly overstated because `refreshOAuthTokens` also requires `CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT` and `userId`, but the core issue (non-boolean flag derived from secrets; enablement coupled to env presence) is grounded in the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The refresh response check uses `response.statusText !== "OK"`, which is locale-dependent and empty for HTTP/2 fetch responses. On Node fetch (undici), statusText for a 200 HTTP/2 response is often an empty string, so every Salesforce refresh throws HttpError 400 even though the token was successfully issued; users on any deployment using HTTP/2 or non-English reason phrases get a broken Salesforce integration.

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/app-store/salesforce/lib/CalendarService.ts`, the new refresh flow checks `if (response.statusText !== "OK") throw new HttpError(...)`. `statusText` is not a reliable success indicator (it can vary by server/reason phrase and may be empty), so a successful 200 response can incorrectly throw. This is a functional defect introduced by the diff; it should use `response.ok` or `response.status` instead.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The webhook handler performs a plain string comparison of the webhook secret header and does not restrict req.method to POST. The shared secret is compared non-constant-time (timing side channel on a credential-writing endpoint), and a GET with the header set proceeds to schema.parse on an undefined body, returning a 500 instead of a 4xx.

adjudication.rationale: In the newly added `apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts` handler there is no `req.method` gate (e.g., `if (req.method !== "POST") ...`). After passing the header secret check, it unconditionally calls `appCredentialWebhookRequestBodySchema.parse(req.body)`, and `zod.parse` will throw on missing/invalid bodies (e.g., GET requests typically have no JSON body), which is uncaught and would surface as a 500. Also, the secret check is a plain `!==` comparison (`req.headers[...] !== process.env.CALCOM_WEBHOOK_SECRET`) rather than a constant-time comparison, which is a verifiable security issue on an endpoint that writes credentials.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] The app-credential webhook authenticates solely with a single shared secret and then writes attacker-supplied keys to any user's credential row, with no per-request scoping, so the credential store for every user is writable by anyone holding that one shared secret. The .env.example instructs operators to distribute CALCOM_WEBHOOK_SECRET across their parent application's admin app settings ('ensure that all app secrets are set the same as the parent application'), multiplying holders of the secret; any one of them (or anyone who reads the admin settings) can POST {userId: <any user>, appSlug, keys} and overwrite/create arbitrary OAuth credentials for any user, then act as that user on the integrated calendar/CRM.

adjudication.rationale: The new API route `apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts` authorizes requests only by checking a single shared secret header (`req.headers[process.env.CALCOM_WEBHOOK_HEADER_NAME||...] === process.env.CALCOM_WEBHOOK_SECRET`). After that, it accepts attacker-controlled `userId`, `appSlug`, and encrypted `keys`, and then updates/creates a credential for `userId` (`prisma.credential.update/create` with `userId: reqBody.userId`) with no additional per-user/per-app scoping or request signing. Therefore anyone who knows the shared secret can overwrite/create credentials for arbitrary users. The `.env.example` guidance to reuse/distribute the same secret across "parent application"/admin app settings further increases the blast radius, consistent with the finding.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] When credential sync is enabled, minimumTokenResponseSchema does not include refresh_token, so the code writes the literal placeholder string "refresh_token" into the parsed data and the calling adapters persist that placeholder into the credential row in the database. GoogleCalendarService (CalendarService.ts ~line 93) and zoom/office365 adapters store {refresh_token: "refresh_token", ...} via prisma.credential.update; any later flow that uses the stored refresh token (e.g. the app is used directly, sync is disabled, or the app is unlinked/relinked) calls the provider's token endpoint with the literal string and the stored credential becomes permanently unusable, forcing re-auth.

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds `parseRefreshTokenResponse`, which when credential sync is enabled (`APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED && CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT`) validates responses using `minimumTokenResponseSchema`. That schema does not include `refresh_token`, and Zod `z.object(...)` will strip unknown keys, so even if the input had a real `refresh_token`, `refreshTokenResponse.data.refresh_token` will be missing. The function then forcibly sets `refreshTokenResponse.data.refresh_token = "refresh_token"`. In `Office365CalendarService`, the returned `tokenResponse.data` is spread into `o365AuthCredentials`, which will overwrite the real stored refresh token with the placeholder and then persist it via `prisma.credential.update`. This matches the finding’s core claim that the placeholder can be stored and break future refresh flows.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The sync fetch to CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT sends calcomUserId and appSlug with no authentication header or signature, and the returned access token is accepted with only the permissive minimumTokenResponseSchema (any access_token string), so token material from the sync endpoint is trusted blindly. A self-hoster pointing CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT at an HTTP (non-TLS) URL, or a MITM on that hop, can inject arbitrary 'access_token' values that are persisted and used as live OAuth tokens for every user of that app — config-backed unvalidated fetch; the fetch is also not gated by APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED's server-side secret checks, only by env presence.

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces `refreshOAuthTokens` which, when `APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED && process.env.CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT && userId` is truthy, POSTs to `CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT` with only `calcomUserId` and `appSlug` in the body and no authentication/signature headers (packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/refreshOAuthTokens.ts). The returned token material is then accepted under a more permissive validation path via `parseRefreshTokenResponse`: when credential sharing + sync endpoint are enabled it uses `minimumTokenResponseSchema` instead of the integration’s stricter schema (packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/parseRefreshTokenResponse.ts), and the resulting token data is used to update persisted credentials (e.g., Office365CalendarService updates prisma credential after `parseRefreshTokenResponse(responseJson, refreshTokenResponseSchema)` in packages/app-store/office365calendar/lib/CalendarService.ts). The diff also does not enforce HTTPS/TLS for `CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT`, so a self-hoster using HTTP or a compromised hop could inject arbitrary `access_token` values that get stored and then used for OAuth calls.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The webhook secret is compared with plain string inequality (req.headers[...] !== process.env.CALCOM_WEBHOOK_SECRET) rather than a constant-time comparison, over an endpoint that grants full credential-write power. An attacker able to measure response-time differences across many requests (network jitter makes this hard but not impossible for a long secret) can recover the shared secret byte-by-byte and then overwrite any user's credentials.

adjudication.rationale: In the newly added webhook handler (`apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts`), the shared secret is validated via a direct string inequality check: `req.headers[process.env.CALCOM_WEBHOOK_HEADER_NAME || "calcom-webhook-secret"] !== process.env.CALCOM_WEBHOOK_SECRET`. This is not a constant-time comparison and the endpoint subsequently decrypts and writes credentials to the database (`prisma.credential.update/create`), so a secret-comparison side channel would impact a high-privilege operation. The finding is directly grounded in the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The decryption uses process.env.CALCOM_APP_CREDENTIAL_ENCRYPTION_KEY || "" with no validation that the key is 32 bytes, despite .env.example stating it must be 32 bytes for AES256, and JSON.parse of symmetricDecrypt output is unguarded. An operator who sets a wrong-length key gets symmetricDecrypt throwing an unhandled 500 on every webhook call (sync silently broken) rather than a startup validation error; an empty-key configuration would attempt decryption with a zero-length key instead of refusing.

adjudication.rationale: In the new webhook handler `apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts`, decryption is done via `symmetricDecrypt(reqBody.keys, process.env.CALCOM_APP_CREDENTIAL_ENCRYPTION_KEY || "")` and immediately `JSON.parse(...)` with no guarding/validation. The only gate is `APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED`, which merely checks the env vars are truthy (no 32-byte length validation as suggested by `.env.example`). A wrong-length/incorrect key or malformed encrypted payload can therefore throw and result in an uncaught 500 rather than a controlled 4xx/clear startup validation. However, the finding’s claim that an empty-key configuration would attempt decryption with a zero-length key is not supported by the diff because `APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED` is falsy for an empty string, so the handler returns 403 before decryption.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] The computed object keys `[z.string().toString()]` and `[z.string().optional().toString()]` evaluate to the literal property name "[object Object]" (Zod schema objects stringify to [object Object]), so minimumTokenResponseSchema requires a numeric property literally named "[object Object]" instead of "allow any other properties". When APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED and CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT are set, every real token refresh response fails minimumTokenResponseSchema.safeParse, throwing "Invalid refreshed tokens were returned" and aborting calendar/video operations for all synced apps (Google, O365, Zoom, Salesforce) — the entire credential-sync feature is unusable, and since the diff contains no tests for parseRefreshTokenResponse, nothing catches this before ship.

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/parseRefreshTokenResponse.ts`, `minimumTokenResponseSchema` is defined with computed keys `[z.string().toString()]` and `[z.string().optional().toString()]`. These evaluate to a single literal property name string (e.g., "[object Object]" or similar), not an “any key”/index signature, so the schema will require a specific property with that exact name rather than accepting arbitrary token-response fields. When `APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED` and `CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT` are set, `parseRefreshTokenResponse` uses this schema and throws on `!success`, which would make real OAuth refresh responses fail parsing and break the refreshed-token flow. The diff also shows multiple integrations now call `parseRefreshTokenResponse`, so this would impact those code paths under the feature flag.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] `refreshTokenResponse.data.refresh_token` is read on the safeParse result without a success check in the branch path — when the schema-parsed result is a ZodSafeParseError, data is undefined, and additionally assigning a fake refresh_token ("refresh_token") on a ZodParsedType object can throw a read-only error in zod. On any token response lacking refresh_token in credential-sync mode, this line throws a TypeError (reading 'refresh_token' of undefined) or an illegal-assignment error, crashing the refresh path with a 500 instead of the intended error message; no test in the diff exercises a response without refresh_token, so the crash ships silently.

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/parseRefreshTokenResponse.ts`, `refreshTokenResponse.data` is only accessed after an explicit `if (!refreshTokenResponse.success) { throw new Error(...) }` guard. That means the code path cannot be a `ZodSafeParseError` with `data === undefined` when it reaches `refreshTokenResponse.data.refresh_token`. The diff also doesn’t show any evidence that `refreshTokenResponse.data` is read-only/frozen such that assigning `refresh_token` would throw. Therefore the finding’s described crash scenario is not supported by what’s in the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] In credential-sync mode refreshOAuthTokens returns a raw fetch Response, but the code immediately reads `res?.data` and then `token.access_token`, which is undefined on a Response — the sync contract ("response should only contain the access token and expiry date") is never actually parsed from the Response body. With credential sync enabled, every Google calendar operation after token expiry sets googleCredentials.access_token to undefined and writes a broken key to prisma.credential, permanently corrupting the stored credential; zero tests in this diff cover the credential-sync branch of refreshOAuthTokens, so this data-corruption path is completely unverified.

adjudication.rationale: In the new sync branch, `refreshOAuthTokens` returns the raw result of `fetch(process.env.CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT, ...)`, i.e. a `Response` object (`packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/refreshOAuthTokens.ts`). But callers like Google Calendar still treat the return as an axios/google-auth style object: `const token = res?.data; googleCredentials.access_token = token.access_token;` (`packages/app-store/googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts`). A `Response` has no `.data`, so in credential-sync mode `token` will be `undefined` (or will throw when reading `token.access_token`), meaning the sync response is never parsed/used. This is a concrete behavioral break introduced by the diff. (The finding's “writes a broken key” part is less directly shown because the code may throw before the Prisma update, but the core incompatibility/incorrect parsing is verifiable.)

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] parseRefreshTokenResponse overwrites refreshTokenResponse.data.refresh_token with the literal string "refresh_token" whenever the payload lacks a refresh_token, and callers persist that result directly into credential.key. Google CalendarService.ts (~line 93) and Office365CalendarService.ts (~line 258) write the parsed object to prisma.credential.update — the user's real OAuth refresh token in the DB is replaced with the junk string "refresh_token", which is irreversible: the stored credential can never be refreshed again and the user must manually re-authorize the app. This also fires in the credential-sync path, where the sync endpoint is documented to return only access_token + expiry, so every synced refresh destroys the stored refresh token.

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/parseRefreshTokenResponse.ts`, when the parsed payload lacks `refresh_token`, the helper forcibly sets `refreshTokenResponse.data.refresh_token = "refresh_token"`. In `packages/app-store/office365calendar/lib/CalendarService.ts`, the returned `tokenResponse.data` is spread into `o365AuthCredentials` (`{ ...o365AuthCredentials, ...(tokenResponse.success && tokenResponse.data) }`), which will overwrite the existing stored `refresh_token` with the literal string when Microsoft (or the credential-sync endpoint) doesn’t return a refresh token. That updated object is then persisted via `prisma.credential.update`, causing irreversible loss of the real refresh token. (Google’s code path passes an object that already contains `refresh_token`, so the overwrite claim is less directly supported there, but the overwrite/persist defect is clearly present for Office365 and any sync responses without `refresh_token`.)

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] minimumTokenResponseSchema uses computed object keys [z.string().toString()] and [z.string().optional().toString()], which evaluate to literal property names "z.string().toString()" / "z.string().optional().toString()", so the schema requires a number-valued property literally named "z.string().toString()". With APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED, safeParse(response) fails for every real token payload (no provider returns such a key), so parseRefreshTokenResponse throws "Invalid refreshed tokens were returned" and the refresh is aborted for Google, Office365, Zoom, and Salesforce — the credential-sync feature this PR adds cannot work at all, and callers like GoogleCalendarService never reach the credential update.

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/parseRefreshTokenResponse.ts`, `minimumTokenResponseSchema` is defined as `z.object({ access_token: z.string(), [z.string().toString()]: z.number(), [z.string().optional().toString()]: z.unknown().optional() })`. In a JS object literal those computed keys evaluate immediately to a single literal string key (whatever `toString()` returns for the Zod object), not a “match any string key” index signature. That means the schema requires a number-valued property with that literal key, so `minimumTokenResponseSchema.safeParse(response)` will fail for normal OAuth token payloads. Since `parseRefreshTokenResponse` selects this schema when `APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED && CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT`, it will throw `"Invalid refreshed tokens were returned"`, breaking the refresh paths updated to call it (e.g., Google/Office365/Zoom/Salesforce).

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] In credential-sync mode refreshOAuthTokens returns a fetch Response while several callers expect an axios response object with a .data property (zoho-bigin CalendarService.ts:91 tokenInfo.data.error, zohocrm CalendarService.ts:213 zohoCrmTokenInfo.data, hubspot CalendarService.ts:184 HubspotToken fields). For Zoho Bigin in sync mode, tokenInfo.data is undefined so !tokenInfo.data.error is true and the very next line tokenInfo.data.expiryDate = ... throws TypeError, crashing booking; for Hubspot, downstream reads like hubspotRefreshToken.refresh_token are undefined and get persisted into credential.key, silently corrupting the stored credential beyond recovery.

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds `refreshOAuthTokens` which, in credential-sync mode (`APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED && process.env.CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT && userId`), performs a `fetch(...)` and returns the raw Fetch `Response` object (packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/refreshOAuthTokens.ts). Multiple callers shown in the diff expect the return value to be an axios/hubspot SDK style object with a `.data` property or direct token fields: e.g. Zoho Bigin `CalendarService.ts` assigns `const tokenInfo = await refreshOAuthTokens(...)` and then immediately uses `tokenInfo.data.error` and later mutates `tokenInfo.data.expiryDate`—but a Fetch `Response` has no `.data`, so in sync mode this will throw at `tokenInfo.data.expiryDate = ...`. Similarly, Zoho CRM uses `zohoCrmTokenInfo.data...` after calling `refreshOAuthTokens(...)`, and Hubspot now assigns `const hubspotRefreshToken: HubspotToken = await refreshOAuthTokens(...)` but would receive a Fetch `Response` in sync mode, not a `HubspotToken` object. This is a concrete, behavior-breaking type/shape mismatch introduced by the new helper.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] The constructor now unconditionally performs a Salesforce token refresh on every service instantiation and gates success on response.statusText !== "OK", which is empty-string for most fetch/undici responses on non-2xx and can be empty even on 2xx depending on runtime. Every Salesforce calendar operation issues a network token refresh before doing any work; when statusText is empty (common under Node 18 fetch), the service throws HttpError 400 and the entire Salesforce integration stops working after this deploy, with no rollback path since the check runs on the hot path.

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/app-store/salesforce/lib/CalendarService.ts`, the new code performs a refresh-token `fetch` immediately after reading `credentialKey` and before returning a `jsforce.Connection`, with no conditional based on token expiry (i.e., it appears to run every time this code path is executed). It also treats any response whose `response.statusText !== "OK"` as an error and throws `HttpError(400)`. The diff does not prove that `statusText` will be empty under the target runtime, but the check is clearly fragile/non-robust compared to `response.ok`/`response.status`, and the unconditional network refresh on a hot path is a significant behavioral concern introduced by the change.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The new constructor refresh persists { ...salesforceTokenSchema fields, refresh_token } to credential.key via a raw spread rather than the app's token type, and does so without the refreshOAuthTokens indirection used by every other app in this PR. Any extra fields previously stored in the Salesforce credential key are silently dropped on the first calendar operation after deploy, and this app bypasses the CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT so self-hosters with credential sharing enabled get inconsistent sync behavior (Salesforce credentials refreshed/persisted locally but never mirrored to the parent app).

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/app-store/salesforce/lib/CalendarService.ts`, the refresh flow is implemented with a direct `fetch(...)` to Salesforce and a direct `prisma.credential.update({ data: { key: { ...accessTokenParsed.data, refresh_token: credentialKey.refresh_token }}})` (new code around the added `salesforceTokenSchema`). This update replaces `credential.key` with only the zod-parsed fields plus `refresh_token`, so any other previously-stored fields on the Salesforce credential are indeed dropped. Also, unlike other apps changed in this PR, Salesforce does not use the new `refreshOAuthTokens(...)` helper, so when `APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED` and `CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT` are set, Salesforce will still refresh/persist locally and will not follow the sync indirection used elsewhere, leading to inconsistent behavior for self-hosters.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] Google's refresh now persists parseRefreshTokenResponse(googleCredentials, ...) instead of schema.parse(googleCredentials) on the pre-existing credential object, so under credential-sharing mode the loose minimum schema replaces the strict googleCredentialSchema validation of the entire stored key. In sharing mode, arbitrary/unvalidated fields from the mutated googleCredentials object (and, once the bogus-computed-key bug is fixed, from any remote response field) are written into credential.key without googleCredentialSchema checking — malformed keys get persisted permanently, and readers of credential.key that assume the Google shape (e.g. expiry_date typing) read misinterpreted data.

adjudication.rationale: In GoogleCalendarService.refreshAccessToken the code now does `const key = parseRefreshTokenResponse(googleCredentials, googleCredentialSchema);` and then persists `key` directly to `prisma.credential.update({ data: { key } })`. But `parseRefreshTokenResponse` returns the Zod `safeParse` result object (with `.success` and `.data`), not the parsed credential payload itself, so this will store the wrong shape into `credential.key`. Additionally, when sharing is enabled, `parseRefreshTokenResponse` intentionally validates against `minimumTokenResponseSchema` instead of `googleCredentialSchema`, so the stored credential no longer receives Google-specific schema validation in that mode (and in this call site it's validating `googleCredentials` rather than the refresh response).

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] parseRefreshTokenResponse silently overwrites a missing refresh_token with the literal string "refresh_token" and callers persist it to the credential row. When the sync endpoint (or any provider) returns a token payload without refresh_token, the bogus string is stored via prisma.credential.update in googlecalendar/office365calendar/zoomvideo; the next refresh sends grant_type=refresh_token with refresh_token="refresh_token" and the provider rejects it, permanently breaking the integration with no log of the original cause.

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/parseRefreshTokenResponse.ts`, the helper explicitly mutates a successful parse result to set `refresh_token` to the literal string `"refresh_token"` when it’s missing: `if (!refreshTokenResponse.data.refresh_token) { refreshTokenResponse.data.refresh_token = "refresh_token"; }`. This can overwrite a previously valid stored refresh token. The diff shows at least one caller that merges the parsed data back into persisted credentials (`office365calendar/lib/CalendarService.ts`: `o365AuthCredentials = { ...o365AuthCredentials, ...(tokenResponse.success && tokenResponse.data) };`), so a missing refresh token in the response would replace the existing one with the bogus string and then be written to the DB on update, breaking future refreshes.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] minimumTokenResponseSchema uses computed keys `[z.string().toString()]` and `[z.string().optional().toString()]`, which evaluate to the literal key "[object Object]"-style strings, so the schema enforces nothing beyond access_token and is structurally meaningless. Every sync-enabled refresh accepts any object containing an access_token (comments imply an expiry number should be required); a response missing expiry leaves expiry_date undefined, googleCredentials.expiry_date becomes undefined, and the token is treated as never-expiring so it is never refreshed again until the API starts returning 401s on user booking paths.

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/parseRefreshTokenResponse.ts`, `minimumTokenResponseSchema` is defined with computed keys like `[z.string().toString()]`, which evaluates to a single literal property name (whatever `toString()` returns, typically a "[object Object]"-style string), not “any string key”. This makes the schema logically wrong (it won’t enforce “any numeric expiry field” as the comment suggests, and may even reject normal token responses if that literal key is absent). This is a real correctness defect introduced by the diff. (The finding’s downstream behavior description about “accepts any object with access_token”/never-expiring tokens isn’t fully verifiable from the diff, but the schema construction itself is plainly incorrect.)

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] In the sync-enabled path refreshOAuthTokens returns a raw fetch Response, but the caller reads `res?.data` expecting the google-auth-librarie's envelope, so `token` is undefined and `token.access_token` throws TypeError. With APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED and CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT set, every Google Calendar token refresh crashes with "Cannot read properties of undefined (access_token)" instead of using the synced token — the feature this diff adds is entirely non-functional for Google Calendar and the failure surfaces as an unhandled error on booking paths.

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/refreshOAuthTokens.ts`, the sync-enabled branch (`APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED && CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT && userId`) returns the raw `fetch(...)` `Response`. But in `packages/app-store/googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts`, the caller treats the returned value like the google-auth-library/gaxios response and does `const token = res?.data;` followed by `token.access_token`. A `fetch` `Response` has no `.data`, so `token` becomes `undefined` and `token.access_token` will throw at runtime when sync is enabled.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] refreshOAuthTokens returns a fetch Response in the sync path but the result is used as a HubspotToken object (hubspotRefreshToken.access_token / expires_in / refresh_token are read off it). In the sync-enabled path all Hubspot token fields are undefined; NaN expiry and undefined tokens get persisted to the credential row, silently corrupting the stored credential so subsequent Hubspot calls fail with invalid-token errors far from the root cause.

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/refreshOAuthTokens.ts`, the sync-enabled branch (`APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED && CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT && userId`) performs a `fetch(...)` and returns the raw `Response` object. In `packages/app-store/hubspot/lib/CalendarService.ts`, `refreshOAuthTokens(...)` is awaited and assigned to `const hubspotRefreshToken: HubspotToken = ...`. That means in the sync path the value is a `Response`, not a `HubspotToken`-shaped object, so any subsequent reads like `hubspotRefreshToken.access_token` / `expires_in` would be wrong (undefined), breaking refresh logic and likely persisting bad credential state.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] In the sync-enabled path tokenInfo is a fetch Response, so `tokenInfo.data` is undefined and `if (!tokenInfo.data.error)` throws TypeError. Every Zoho Bigin credential refresh with sync enabled crashes before the credential is persisted, so the synced access token is never used and the integration breaks with an unhandled TypeError.

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/app-store/zoho-bigin/lib/CalendarService.ts`, the refresh logic was changed to call `refreshOAuthTokens(...)` and then still treats the result like an Axios response (`tokenInfo.data.error`). But `refreshOAuthTokens` returns a `fetch(...)` `Response` object when `APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED && process.env.CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT && userId` is truthy (see `packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/refreshOAuthTokens.ts`). A `Response` does not have a `.data` property, so `tokenInfo.data` will be `undefined` and `tokenInfo.data.error` will throw a `TypeError` in the sync-enabled path, breaking Zoho Bigin token refresh.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] The userId argument passed to refreshOAuthTokens is `credentialId`, not the user's id, so the sync endpoint receives a credential id as calcomUserId. The parent application looks up the wrong user (or no user) by credential id and returns wrong or missing tokens — every synced Zoho Bigin refresh operates on the wrong identity with no error surfaced.

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/app-store/zoho-bigin/lib/CalendarService.ts`, the refresh path calls `refreshOAuthTokens(..., "zoho-bigin", credentialId)`, whereas `refreshOAuthTokens`’s third parameter is `userId` and is sent to the sync endpoint as `calcomUserId` (see `packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/refreshOAuthTokens.ts`). Passing a credential identifier instead of `credential.userId` will cause the sync endpoint to receive the wrong user id and refresh tokens for the wrong/missing identity.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] In the sync-enabled path zohoCrmTokenInfo is a fetch Response, so `zohoCrmTokenInfo.data` is undefined and `if (!zohoCrmTokenInfo.data.error)` throws TypeError. Every Zoho CRM refresh with sync enabled crashes with an unhandled TypeError instead of using the synced token.

adjudication.rationale: `refreshOAuthTokens` returns a `fetch(...)` `Response` object when `APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED && process.env.CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT && userId` (see `packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/refreshOAuthTokens.ts`). In `packages/app-store/zohocrm/lib/CalendarService.ts`, the refreshed token call is wrapped with `refreshOAuthTokens(...)` but the subsequent logic still assumes an Axios response (`zohoCrmTokenInfo.data.error`, `zohoCrmTokenInfo.data.expiryDate`, etc.). If the sync path is taken, `zohoCrmTokenInfo.data` is `undefined`, so `zohoCrmTokenInfo.data.error` will throw a `TypeError` at runtime. This matches the finding’s described crash in the sync-enabled path.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] Success is checked via `response.statusText !== "OK"` instead of response.ok; under HTTP/2 (or proxies) statusText is empty, and Salesforce may return lowercase "ok", so the check throws HttpError 400 on a successful refresh or accepts based on a non-normative field. Salesforce integrations refresh successfully but throw "Bad Request-style" 400 errors (empty statusText under HTTP/2 fetch), or a 5xx response with statusText "OK" slips through and its body is parsed as a token.

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/app-store/salesforce/lib/CalendarService.ts`, the new refresh-token fetch checks success via `if (response.statusText !== "OK") throw new HttpError(...)` instead of using `response.ok` / `response.status`. This is diff-grounded and can misclassify successful responses when `statusText` is empty or non-standard, causing erroneous 400s, and can also allow non-2xx responses through if `statusText` happens to be "OK".

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] The dead check `if (!accessTokenParsed.success)` can never fire because parseRefreshTokenResponse already throws on failure; meanwhile a brand-new unconditional Salesforce token fetch+DB write now runs on every service construction regardless of whether the token is expired. Every SalesforceCalendarService instantiation (every booking operation touching Salesforce) now performs an extra outbound login.salesforce.com POST plus a prisma.credential.update, a hot-path regression that also writes the credential row on every call — and a transient Salesforce outage turns previously-working cached-token operations into hard failures at construction time.

adjudication.rationale: In `SalesforceCalendarService` a refresh-token POST to `https://login.salesforce.com/services/oauth2/token` plus `prisma.credential.update(...)` is now executed unconditionally during service construction (no expiry check/guard), so every instantiation performs an outbound call and DB write on the hot path. Also, `parseRefreshTokenResponse(...)` throws when parsing fails, so the subsequent check `if (!accessTokenParsed.success)` is dead/unreachable in this code path.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] In the sync-enabled path the raw fetch Response from the sync endpoint is passed to handleLarkError, which expects a Lark-shaped {code, msg, data} envelope from LARK_HOST. handleLarkError throws (or returns no data) because the sync endpoint's minimal {access_token, expiry} payload has no Lark code field, so every Lark refresh with sync enabled fails and no token is persisted.

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/app-store/larkcalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts`, the refresh call is now wrapped with `refreshOAuthTokens(...)` and the returned `resp` is always passed into `handleLarkError<RefreshTokenResp>(resp, ...)`. But `refreshOAuthTokens`’s sync-enabled branch returns a `fetch()` response from `process.env.CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT` (with a comment that it returns only access token + expiry), not Lark’s `/authen/v1/refresh_access_token` response. The code does not add any adapter (unlike other integrations that use `parseRefreshTokenResponse`), so if `handleLarkError` expects Lark’s response shape, the sync path will fail for Lark token refresh.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The sync-endpoint fetch has no timeout and never checks response.ok/status before the result is consumed as a token response. A slow or hanging credential-sync endpoint stalls every calendar/video operation (booking flows) indefinitely with no error, and a 500 HTML error body from the endpoint flows into token parsing where it produces a confusing "Invalid refreshed tokens were returned" instead of surfacing the HTTP failure.

adjudication.rationale: In the newly added `packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/refreshOAuthTokens.ts`, the sync-path does `fetch(process.env.CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT, { method: "POST", body: new URLSearchParams(...) })` and immediately `return response;` with no timeout/abort mechanism and no `response.ok`/status handling. This means if the credential-sync endpoint is slow/hangs, callers awaiting token refresh (e.g., multiple `CalendarService`/`VideoApiAdapter` refresh flows updated to call `refreshOAuthTokens`) can block indefinitely. Also, because no HTTP failure is detected at this layer, downstream code may only fail later during token parsing/handling, surfacing generic token-validation errors rather than the actual HTTP error from the sync endpoint.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] appCredentialWebhookRequestBodySchema.parse, symmetricDecrypt, and JSON.parse are all unguarded, so malformed bodies or bad encryption throw and Next returns a raw 500 instead of the 4xx the endpoint's own contract (403/404) style promises. A sender with the valid webhook secret but a misencrypted keys payload (e.g. key env differs between systems — exactly the cross-system setup this endpoint serves) gets an opaque 500 with no indication whether the failure was decryption vs. JSON vs. schema, instead of a 400 naming the problem.

adjudication.rationale: In the new API route `apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts`, the handler calls `appCredentialWebhookRequestBodySchema.parse(req.body)`, `symmetricDecrypt(...)`, and `JSON.parse(...)` without any try/catch or use of `safeParse`. Any malformed body, wrong encryption key, or non-JSON plaintext will throw and bubble up, resulting in an unhandled exception (raw 500) rather than a controlled 4xx response like the rest of the endpoint (which explicitly returns 403/404). This is directly verifiable from the added code paths and is especially likely in the intended cross-system setup when env keys differ.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] When CALCOM_WEBHOOK_SECRET is unset, `req.headers[...] === process.env.CALCOM_WEBHOOK_SECRET` compares undefined to undefined and passes. On a deployment where APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED is truthily set via some other means (or where the env wiring drifts from the constants.ts derivation), the secret check silently becomes a no-op that accepts every request; the current constants.ts guard makes this latent, but the endpoint itself does not fail closed.

adjudication.rationale: In `apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts`, the secret check is `req.headers[...] !== process.env.CALCOM_WEBHOOK_SECRET`; if `CALCOM_WEBHOOK_SECRET` is `undefined` and the header is absent, this comparison will evaluate as `undefined !== undefined` (false) and therefore *not* reject. However, in this diff the handler is preceded by `if (!APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED) return 403`, and `APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED` is defined in `packages/lib/constants.ts` as `process.env.CALCOM_WEBHOOK_SECRET && process.env.CALCOM_APP_CREDENTIAL_ENCRYPTION_KEY`, which makes the route unreachable when the secret is unset. So it’s not a currently-triggerable defect given the diff, but it is a valid, diff-grounded hardening concern (the endpoint itself doesn’t explicitly fail closed on missing envs).

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] On sync-enabled refreshes, minimumTokenResponseSchema accepts a payload without refresh_token and the parseRefreshTokenResponse default injects refresh_token="refresh_token", which is then spread into o365AuthCredentials and persisted via prisma.credential.update. The Office365 credential row is overwritten with a garbage refresh_token on the first sync-enabled refresh; the next refresh sends that garbage to Microsoft, which rejects it, and the integration is permanently broken with the root cause invisible in logs (the previous console.error for parse failures was also deleted).

adjudication.rationale: In sync-enabled mode, `parseRefreshTokenResponse` deliberately tolerates responses without `refresh_token` (it uses `minimumTokenResponseSchema` when `APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED && CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT`), and then mutates the parsed data to inject `refresh_token = "refresh_token"` when missing. In `Office365CalendarService`, the returned safe-parse object is used to merge `tokenResponse.data` into `o365AuthCredentials` (`{ ...o365AuthCredentials, ...(tokenResponse.success && tokenResponse.data) }`), which will overwrite the existing valid `refresh_token` with the injected garbage value, and that updated credential object is then persisted via `prisma.credential.update`. This is a real data-corruption path introduced by the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] In the sync-enabled path the Response from the minimal sync endpoint is passed to handleWebexResponse and its parsed body is used as a Webex token (access_token, refresh_token, expires_in expected), but the sync endpoint by contract returns only access token and expiry. refresh_token and expires_in are undefined on the synced payload, so the persisted Webex credential lacks a refresh token and expiry arithmetic yields NaN, breaking subsequent MS-Teams/Webex meeting creation with no error pointing at the sync path.

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/app-store/webex/lib/VideoApiAdapter.ts`, the refresh flow now routes through `refreshOAuthTokens(...)`. In the sync-enabled branch (`APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED && CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT && userId`), `refreshOAuthTokens` performs a POST to the sync endpoint and returns that `Response` (see `packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/refreshOAuthTokens.ts`), with comments stating the sync endpoint “should only contain the access token and expiry date”. The Webex adapter then passes this response to `handleWebexResponse(response, credential.id)` and continues as if it were a normal Webex token refresh response. Unlike Zoom/Office365/Google, Webex does not use `parseRefreshTokenResponse` (added specifically to tolerate minimal token responses and patch missing `refresh_token`), so a minimal synced payload can lack fields Webex token handling likely relies on (e.g., `refresh_token`, `expires_in`). This mismatch is introduced by the diff and can break subsequent use when those fields are assumed present.
